knowledge_points.name: Humanist Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Humanists, including theorists Abraham Maslow (1908–1970) and Carl Rogers (1902–1987), stressed individual choice and free will.
knowledge_points.plain: 强调自由选择与个人成长

knowledge_points.name: Psychodynamic Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychologists using this perspective believe that the unconscious mind—a part of our mind that we do not have conscious control over or access to—controls much of our thought and action.
knowledge_points.plain: 强调无意识对行为的控制

knowledge_points.name: Biopsychology (or Neuroscience) Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Biopsychologists explain human thought and behavior strictly in terms of biological processes.
knowledge_points.plain: 用生物过程解释心理行为

knowledge_points.name: Evolutionary (or Darwinian) Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Evolutionary psychologists (also sometimes called sociobiologists) examine human thoughts and actions in terms of natural selection.
knowledge_points.plain: 从自然选择角度解释心理

knowledge_points.name: Behavioral Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Behaviorists explain human thought and behavior in terms of conditioning.
knowledge_points.plain: 用条件作用解释行为

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cognitive psychologists examine human thought and behavior in terms of how we interpret, process, and remember environmental events.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究人如何解释与记忆信息

knowledge_points.name: Social-Cultural (or Sociocultural) Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social-cultural psychologists look at how our thoughts and behaviors vary among cultures.
knowledge_points.plain: 关注文化如何影响思想行为

knowledge_points.name: Biopsychosocial Perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This modern perspective acknowledges that human thinking and behavior results from combinations of biological (“bio”), psychological (“psycho”), and social (“social”) factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 生物心理社会因素共同作用

knowledge_points.name: eclectic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This point of view, sometimes called eclectic, claims that no one perspective has all the answers to the variety of human thought and behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 综合多种视角解释心理现象

knowledge_points.name: Hindsight bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People have the tendency upon hearing about research findings (and many other things) to think that they knew it all along; this tendency is called hindsight bias.
knowledge_points.plain: 高估自己事前已知的倾向

knowledge_points.name: Confirmation bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Confirmation bias is the tendency to pay more attention to information that supports our preexisting ideas
knowledge_points.plain: 只关注支持既有想法的信息

knowledge_points.name: Overconfidence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: overconfidence is the tendency to be, well, overconfident about the things we believe
knowledge_points.plain: 高估自己判断的准确性

knowledge_points.name: Applied research
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This type of research is known as applied research because it has clear, practical applications.
knowledge_points.plain: 有明确实际应用的研究

knowledge_points.name: Basic research
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Basic research explores questions that are of interest to psychologists but are not intended to have immediate, real-world applications.
knowledge_points.plain: 不以即时应用为目的的研究

knowledge_points.name: Quantitative research
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Quantitative research uses numerical measures
knowledge_points.plain: 使用数值测量的研究

knowledge_points.name: Qualitative research
knowledge_points.definition_quote: qualitative research typically uses more complex textual responses and looks for key themes within them.
knowledge_points.plain: 分析文本主题的研究

knowledge_points.name: Hypothesis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A hypothesis expresses a relationship between two variables.
knowledge_points.plain: 表述两个变量间的关系

knowledge_points.name: Variables
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Variables, by definition, are things that can vary among the participants in the research.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究中可变化的因素

knowledge_points.name: Experimental hypothesis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: According to an experimental hypothesis, the dependent variable depends on the independent variable.
knowledge_points.plain: 因变量取决于自变量

knowledge_points.name: Independent variable
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In this hypothesis, watching television violence is the independent variable since the hypothesis suggests that a change in television viewing will result in a change in behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究者操纵的变量

knowledge_points.name: Dependent variable
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In testing a hypothesis, researchers manipulate the independent variable and measure the dependent variable.
knowledge_points.plain: 实验中测量到的结果变量

knowledge_points.name: Theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A theory aims to explain some phenomenon and allows researchers to generate testable hypotheses with the hope of collecting data that support the theory.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释现象并生成假设

knowledge_points.name: Falsifiable
knowledge_points.definition_quote: It is essential the hypotheses be falsifiable; that is, it must be possible to gather data that would controvert the hypothesis.
knowledge_points.plain: 可被数据否定的性质

knowledge_points.name: Operational definitions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When you operationalize a variable, you explain how you will measure it.
knowledge_points.plain: 说明变量如何测量

knowledge_points.name: Validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Research is valid when it measures what the researcher set out to measure; it is accurate.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究测量到所测内容

knowledge_points.name: Reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Research is reliable when it can be replicated; it is consistent.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究结果可重复且一致

knowledge_points.name: Sampling
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The individuals on which the research will be conducted are called participants (or subjects), and the process by which participants are selected is called sampling.
knowledge_points.plain: 从总体中选取参与者的过程

knowledge_points.name: Population
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The population includes anyone or anything that could possibly be selected to be in the sample.
knowledge_points.plain: 可能被选取的全部对象

knowledge_points.name: Representative sample
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The goal in selecting a sample is that it be representative of a larger population.
knowledge_points.plain: 能代表总体的样本

knowledge_points.name: Random sampling
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The definition of random sampling is that every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected.
knowledge_points.plain: 人人机会均等的抽样

knowledge_points.name: Convenience sampling
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Using my own students for the research is an example of convenience sampling, collecting data from a group of people who are easily accessible to you.
knowledge_points.plain: 选取易接触人群的抽样

knowledge_points.name: Stratified sampling
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Stratified sampling is a process that allows a researcher to ensure that the sample represents the population on some criteria.
knowledge_points.plain: 按比例分层抽取样本

knowledge_points.name: Confounding variable
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A confounding variable is any difference between the experimental and control conditions, except for the independent variable, that might affect the dependent variable.
knowledge_points.plain: 自变量之外影响因变量的差异

knowledge_points.name: Random assignment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Random assignment means that each participant has an equal chance of being placed into either group.
knowledge_points.plain: 等概率分配参与者入组

knowledge_points.name: Group matching
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If one wanted to ensure that the experimental and control groups were equivalent on some criterion (e.g., sex, IQ scores, age), one could use group matching.
knowledge_points.plain: 按特征匹配实验与控制组

knowledge_points.name: Experimenter bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Experimenter bias is the unconscious tendency for researchers to treat members of the experimental and control groups differently to increase the chance of confirming the researchers' hypothesis.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究者无意识区别对待各组

knowledge_points.name: Double-blind study
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A double-blind study occurs when neither the participants nor the researcher are able to affect the outcome of the research.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究者和参与者都不知情

knowledge_points.name: Single-blind study
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A single-blind study occurs when only the participants do not know to which group they have been assigned; this strategy minimizes the effect of demand characteristics as well as certain kinds of response or participant bias.
knowledge_points.plain: 仅参与者不知所在组别

knowledge_points.name: Demand characteristics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Demand characteristics are cues about the purpose of the study.
knowledge_points.plain: 提示研究目的的线索

knowledge_points.name: Experimental group
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The experimental group is the one that gets the treatment operationalized in the independent variable.
knowledge_points.plain: 接受实验处理的组

knowledge_points.name: Control group
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The control group gets none of the independent variable.
knowledge_points.plain: 不接受实验处理的比较组

knowledge_points.name: Placebo method
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Whenever participants in the experimental group are supposed to ingest a drug, participants in the control group are given an inert but otherwise identical substance.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制组服用无活性物质

knowledge_points.name: Correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A correlation expresses a relationship between two variables without ascribing cause.
knowledge_points.plain: 两个变量间的关系

knowledge_points.name: Positive correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A positive correlation between two things means that the presence of one thing predicts the presence of the other.
knowledge_points.plain: 一个出现预示另一个出现

knowledge_points.name: Negative correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A negative correlation means that the presence of one thing predicts the absence of the other.
knowledge_points.plain: 一个出现预示另一个不出现

knowledge_points.name: Ex post facto (quasi-experimental) study
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If I seek to control all other aspects of the research process, as I would in an experiment, I will have conducted an ex post facto (quasi-experimental) study.
knowledge_points.plain: 无法确定因果的准实验

knowledge_points.name: Survey method
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The survey method, as common sense suggests, involves asking people to fill out surveys.
knowledge_points.plain: 让参与者填写问卷

knowledge_points.name: Likert scales
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One common type of item used on surveys are Likert scales, which pose a statement and ask people to express their level of agreement/disagreement with the statement.
knowledge_points.plain: 测量同意程度的量表

knowledge_points.name: Directionality problem
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The inability to tell which of the variables came first (also known as temporal precedence) is called the directionality problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 无法判断变量先后顺序

knowledge_points.name: Spurious correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In this case, there is no real relationship between the two variables being studied at all, and the correlation is known as a spurious (false) correlation.
knowledge_points.plain: 第三变量导致的虚假相关

knowledge_points.name: Naturalistic observation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sometimes researchers opt to observe participants in their natural habitats without interacting with them at all.
knowledge_points.plain: 在自然环境中不干预地观察

knowledge_points.name: Qualitative data
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although many surveys are comprised of items that participants select from a set of choices, they also can include open-ended questions where participants can write in their responses; this type of data are qualitative.
knowledge_points.plain: 开放式文本形式的资料

knowledge_points.name: Structured interview
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A structured interview is like a survey in that there are fixed number of questions asked in a set order.
knowledge_points.plain: 固定问题与顺序的访谈

knowledge_points.name: Semistructured or unstructured interviews
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, interviews can also be semistructured or unstructured, allowing more opportunity for the interviewer to react to the participants' responses and obtain a richer, albeit less controlled, set of data.
knowledge_points.plain: 允许灵活追问的访谈

knowledge_points.name: Case study method
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The case study method is used to get a full, detailed picture of one participant or a small group of participants.
knowledge_points.plain: 深入描述个案的研究

knowledge_points.name: Science Practice 3—Data Analysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Specifically, in this section you will learn about what the College Board calls Science Practice 3—Data Analysis: understanding and making inferences based on numerical data.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据数值数据进行推断

knowledge_points.name: Descriptive statistics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Descriptive statistics, as the name suggests, simply describe a set of data.
knowledge_points.plain: 概括描述数据的统计

knowledge_points.name: Mean
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The mean is what we usually refer to as the average of all the scores in a distribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 全部得分的算术平均

knowledge_points.name: Median
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The median is the central score in the distribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 分布中居中的分数

knowledge_points.name: Mode
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The mode is the score that appears most frequently.
knowledge_points.plain: 出现次数最多的分数

knowledge_points.name: Positively skewed distribution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When a distribution includes an extreme score (or group of scores) that is very high, as in the car example above, the distribution is said to be positively skewed.
knowledge_points.plain: 极端高值造成正偏态

knowledge_points.name: Negatively skewed distribution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When the skew is caused by a particularly low score (or group of scores), the distribution is negatively skewed.
knowledge_points.plain: 极端低值造成负偏态

knowledge_points.name: Range
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The range is the distance between the highest and lowest scores in a distribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 最高分与最低分之差

knowledge_points.name: Standard deviation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The variance and standard deviation are closely related; standard deviation is simply the square root of the variance.
knowledge_points.plain: 衡量分数离散程度

knowledge_points.name: z-scores
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These z-scores measure the distance of a score from the mean in units of standard deviation.
knowledge_points.plain: 以标准差为单位表示距均值

knowledge_points.name: Normal curve
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The normal curve is a theoretical bell-shaped curve for which the area under the curve lying between any two z-scores has been predetermined.
knowledge_points.plain: 钟形理论分布曲线

knowledge_points.name: Percentiles
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Someone who scores in the 90th percentile on a test has scored better than 90 percent of the people who took the test.
knowledge_points.plain: 表示低于某分数者比例

knowledge_points.name: Correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A correlation measures the relationship between two variables.
knowledge_points.plain: 衡量两个变量的关系

knowledge_points.name: Positive correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If two things are positively correlated, the presence of one thing predicts the presence of the other.
knowledge_points.plain: 一个出现预示另一个出现

knowledge_points.name: Negative correlation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In contrast, a negative correlation means that the presence of one thing predicts the absence of the other.
knowledge_points.plain: 一个出现预示另一个不出现

knowledge_points.name: Correlation coefficient
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The strength of a correlation can be computed by a statistic called the correlation coefficient.
knowledge_points.plain: 表示相关强度的数值

knowledge_points.name: Scatterplot
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A scatterplot graphs pairs of values, one on the y-axis and one on the x-axis.
knowledge_points.plain: 用点显示成对数值

knowledge_points.name: Line of best fit
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The line of best fit, or regression line, is the line drawn through the scatter plot that minimizes the distance of all the points from the line.
knowledge_points.plain: 最贴合散点数据的直线

knowledge_points.name: Inferential statistics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Whereas descriptive statistics provide a way to summarize information about the sample studied, the purpose of inferential statistics is to determine whether findings can be applied to the larger population from which the sample was selected.
knowledge_points.plain: 将样本结果推广到总体

knowledge_points.name: Sampling error
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The extent to which the sample differs from the population is known as sampling error.
knowledge_points.plain: 样本与总体的差异

knowledge_points.name: p-value
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The p-value gives the probability that the difference between the groups is due to chance.
knowledge_points.plain: 结果由偶然造成的概率

knowledge_points.name: Statistical significance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Scientists have decided that a p-value of 0.05 is the cutoff for statistically significant results.
knowledge_points.plain: 结果不太可能出于偶然

knowledge_points.name: Practical significance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In addition to statistical significance, psychologists are interested in practical significance—or how large an effect is.
knowledge_points.plain: 效应在实际中的大小

knowledge_points.name: Replication
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When we replicate a study, we conduct it again using the same methodology in an attempt to see if the results will be the same.
knowledge_points.plain: 重复研究检验结果

knowledge_points.name: Meta-analysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Meta-analysis is a type of research that combines the results of many studies on the same topic in order to approximate an average effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 合并多项研究求平均效应

knowledge_points.name: Peer review
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Prior to publication, psychology studies undergo peer review, a process by which a paper is read by several others in the field and the author is asked to make revisions in order to ensure high quality publications.
knowledge_points.plain: 发表前的同行评审

knowledge_points.name: Institutional review board (IRB)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Any type of academic research must first propose the study to the ethics board or institutional review board (IRB) at the institution.
knowledge_points.plain: 审查研究伦理的机构

knowledge_points.name: Clear scientific purpose
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The research must have a clear scientific purpose.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究须有明确科学目的

knowledge_points.name: Least amount of suffering feasible
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researchers must design experimental procedures that employ the least amount of suffering feasible.
knowledge_points.plain: 尽量减少动物痛苦

knowledge_points.name: No coercion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: No coercion—Participation should be voluntary.
knowledge_points.plain: 参与必须完全自愿

knowledge_points.name: Informed consent
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Informed consent—Participants must know that they are involved in research and give their consent.
knowledge_points.plain: 知情并自愿同意参与

knowledge_points.name: Confidentiality (or anonymity)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Confidentiality (or anonymity)—Participants’ privacy must be protected.
knowledge_points.plain: 保护参与者隐私身份

knowledge_points.name: Risk
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Risk—Participants cannot be placed at significant mental or physical risk; they must have protection from harm.
knowledge_points.plain: 避免严重身心伤害

knowledge_points.name: Debriefing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Debriefing—After the study, participants should be told the purpose of the study and provided with ways to contact the researchers about the results.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究后说明目的结果

knowledge_points.name: Neuroscience or biopsychological perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The influence of biology (sometimes called the neuroscience or biopsychological perspective) is growing.
knowledge_points.plain: 从生物学角度研究心理的视角

knowledge_points.name: Genetic predisposition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The term genetic predisposition refers to the increased chance of developing a specific trait or condition due to our genetic code.
knowledge_points.plain: 基因带来的特质或疾病易感性

knowledge_points.name: DNA
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The genetic material that makes up chromosomes is DNA—deoxyribonucleic acid.
knowledge_points.plain: 构成染色体的遗传物质

knowledge_points.name: Genes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Certain segments of DNA control the production of specific proteins that control some human traits. These discrete segments are called genes.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制特定蛋白质合成的DNA片段

knowledge_points.name: Dominant or recessive genes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Genes can be dominant or recessive. If we inherit two recessive genes for a particular trait, that trait is expressed. In any other combination of genes, the dominant trait is expressed.
knowledge_points.plain: 显性基因表达，隐性需成对才表达

knowledge_points.name: Identical twins (monozygotic twins)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Since identical twins (called monozygotic twins since they develop from one fertilized egg called a zygote) share all the same genetic material, researchers study them in order to examine the influence of genes on human traits.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一受精卵发育、基因相同

knowledge_points.name: Chromosomal abnormality
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Occasionally, chromosomes will combine (or fail to) in an unusual way, resulting in a chromosomal abnormality.
knowledge_points.plain: 染色体组合异常导致的状况

knowledge_points.name: Turner’s syndrome
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For example, babies with Turner’s syndrome are born with only a single X chromosome in the spot usually occupied by the 23rd pair.
knowledge_points.plain: 只有一条X染色体的异常

knowledge_points.name: Klinefelter’s syndrome
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Babies born with Klinefelter’s syndrome have an extra X chromosome, resulting in an XXY pattern.
knowledge_points.plain: 多一条X染色体，呈XXY

knowledge_points.name: Down syndrome
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Babies with Down syndrome are born with an extra chromosome on the 21st pair.
knowledge_points.plain: 第21对染色体多出一条

knowledge_points.name: Neuroanatomy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Neuroanatomy refers to the study of the parts and function of neurons.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究神经元结构与功能

knowledge_points.name: Neurons
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Neurons are individual nerve cells.
knowledge_points.plain: 神经系统的单个神经细胞

knowledge_points.name: Dendrites
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Dendrites—rootlike parts of the cell that stretch out from the cell body.
knowledge_points.plain: 从胞体伸出的根状部分

knowledge_points.name: Cell body (soma)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cell body (also called the soma)—contains the nucleus and other parts of the cell needed to sustain its life.
knowledge_points.plain: 含细胞核的神经元主体

knowledge_points.name: Axon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Axon—wirelike structure ending in the terminal buttons that extends from the cell body.
knowledge_points.plain: 从胞体延伸至末梢的线状结构

knowledge_points.name: Myelin sheath
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Myelin sheath—a fatty covering around the axon of some neurons that speeds neural impulses.
knowledge_points.plain: 包裹轴突、加速传导的脂肪层

knowledge_points.name: Terminal buttons
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Terminal buttons (also called end buttons, terminal branches of axons, and synaptic knobs)—the branched end of the axon that contain neurotransmitters.
knowledge_points.plain: 轴突末端、储存递质

knowledge_points.name: Synapse
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Synapse—the space between the terminal buttons of one neuron and the dendrites of the next neuron.
knowledge_points.plain: 两个神经元之间的间隙

knowledge_points.name: Neurotransmitters
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Neurotransmitters—chemicals contained in terminal buttons that enable neurons to communicate.
knowledge_points.plain: 神经元间传递信息的化学物质

knowledge_points.name: Resting potential
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In its resting state (also referred to as resting potential), a neuron has an overall slightly negative charge (–70 mV) because mostly negative ions are within the cell and mostly positive ions are surrounding it.
knowledge_points.plain: 静息时神经元内负外正

knowledge_points.name: Threshold
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If enough neurotransmitters are received (this level is called the threshold), the cell membrane of neuron B becomes permeable and positive ions rush into the cell, bringing the charge within the cell to approximately +40 mV.
knowledge_points.plain: 触发神经元放电的临界刺激量

knowledge_points.name: Action potential
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The change in charge spreads down the length of neuron B. This electric message firing is called an action potential.
knowledge_points.plain: 神经元传导的电冲动

knowledge_points.name: All-or-none principle
knowledge_points.definition_quote: It’s important to note that a neuron either fires completely or does not fire; this is called the all-or-none principle.
knowledge_points.plain: 神经元要么全放电要么不放电

knowledge_points.name: Depolarization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This process of neural firing is also called depolarization because the cell fires due to the resting potential of the cell—its negative charge—becoming “depolarized” when positive ions rush into the cell, changing the overall charge from negative to positive.
knowledge_points.plain: 正离子内流使膜电位变正

knowledge_points.name: Excitatory neurotransmitters
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some neurotransmitters are excitatory, meaning that they excite the next cell into firing.
knowledge_points.plain: 促使下一个神经元放电

knowledge_points.name: Inhibitory neurotransmitters
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Other neurotransmitters are inhibitory, meaning that they inhibit the next cell from firing.
knowledge_points.plain: 抑制下一个神经元放电

knowledge_points.name: Sensory neurons (afferent neurons)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sensory neurons, or afferent neurons, take information from the senses to the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 把感官信息传向大脑

knowledge_points.name: Interneurons (association neurons)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Once information reaches the brain or spinal cord, interneurons (also called association neurons) take the messages and send them elsewhere in the brain or on to efferent neurons.
knowledge_points.plain: 中枢内连接感觉与运动神经元

knowledge_points.name: Motor neurons (efferent neurons)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Motor neurons, or efferent neurons, take information from the brain to the rest of the body.
knowledge_points.plain: 把指令从大脑传到身体

knowledge_points.name: Organization of the Nervous System
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our nervous system is divided into different categories based on function. The two main divisions are the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system.
knowledge_points.plain: 中枢与周围两大神经系统

knowledge_points.name: Central nervous system (CNS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The central nervous system (CNS) consists of our brain and spinal cord—all the nerves housed within bone (the skull and vertebrae).
knowledge_points.plain: 脑和脊髓组成的中枢系统

knowledge_points.name: Spinal cord
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The spinal cord is a bundle of nerves that run through the center of the spine.
knowledge_points.plain: 贯穿脊柱的神经束

knowledge_points.name: Afferent nerves
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sensory neurons in your toe are activated, and this message is transmitted up a neuron that runs from your toe to the base of your spine (afferent nerves).
knowledge_points.plain: 把感觉信息传向中枢的神经

knowledge_points.name: Reflex arcs
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, humans have a few reflexes that work differently: reflex arcs. Certain reactions occur the moment sensory impulses reach the spinal cord.
knowledge_points.plain: 脊髓直接完成的不随意反应

knowledge_points.name: Peripheral nervous system (PNS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The peripheral nervous system (PNS) consists of all the nerves in your body that are not part of the central nervous system—that is, all the nerves not encased in bone.
knowledge_points.plain: 中枢以外、未包在骨内的神经

knowledge_points.name: Somatic nervous system
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The somatic nervous system controls our voluntary muscle movements.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制随意肌肉运动

knowledge_points.name: Autonomic nervous system
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The autonomic nervous system controls the automatic functions of our body—our heart, lungs, internal organs, glands, and so on.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制心跳、内脏等自动功能

knowledge_points.name: Fight-or-flight response
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These nerves control our responses to stress: the fight-or-flight response that prepares our body to respond to a perceived threat.
knowledge_points.plain: 应对威胁的应激准备反应

knowledge_points.name: Sympathetic nervous system
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The sympathetic nervous system mobilizes our body to respond to stress.
knowledge_points.plain: 动员身体应对压力

knowledge_points.name: Parasympathetic nervous system
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The parasympathetic nervous system has the opposite job of the sympathetic system. It carries messages to the stress response system that cause many of our body activities to slow down and return the body to homeostasis (its typical level) after a stress response.
knowledge_points.plain: 使身体平静并恢复稳态

knowledge_points.name: Endocrine system
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another part of human biology relevant to psychology is the endocrine system. This is a system of glands that secrete hormones that affect many different biological processes in our bodies.
knowledge_points.plain: 分泌激素调节身体机能

knowledge_points.name: Adrenal glands
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The adrenal glands produce adrenaline (also known as epinephrine), which signals the rest of the body to prepare for fight or flight.
knowledge_points.plain: 分泌肾上腺素应对压力

knowledge_points.name: Ovaries and testes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Ovaries and testes produce our sex hormones, estrogen for females and testosterone for males.
knowledge_points.plain: 分泌雌激素与雄激素

knowledge_points.name: Ways of Studying the Brain
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As mentioned previously, the first challenge of brain research is creating a way of detecting brain function.
knowledge_points.plain: 检测脑功能的研究方法

knowledge_points.name: Accidents
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Accidents like this give researchers clues about brain function.
knowledge_points.plain: 借事故损伤推断脑功能

knowledge_points.name: Phineas Gage
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In 1848, a railroad worker named Phineas Gage was involved in an accident that damaged the front part of his brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 脑损伤改变情绪与冲动的案例

knowledge_points.name: Lesioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Lesioning is the removal or destruction of part of the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 切除或破坏部分脑组织

knowledge_points.name: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An electroencephalogram (EEG) detects brain waves.
knowledge_points.plain: 记录脑电波的技术

knowledge_points.name: Computerized axial tomography (CAT or CT) scan
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A computerized axial tomography (CAT or CT) scan is a sophisticated X ray.
knowledge_points.plain: 用X射线呈现脑结构

knowledge_points.name: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is similar to a CAT scan in a way: both scans give you pictures of the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 用磁场生成详细脑结构图

knowledge_points.name: Positron emission tomography (PET) scan
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A positron emission tomography (PET) scan lets researchers see what areas of the brain are most active during certain tasks.
knowledge_points.plain: 显示脑区活动水平

knowledge_points.name: Functional MRI (fMRI)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Functional MRI (fMRI) is a technology that combines elements of the MRI and PET scans.
knowledge_points.plain: 结合结构与血流的脑成像

knowledge_points.name: Brain Structure and Function
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When you study the brain, think about three separate major categories or sections: hindbrain, midbrain, and forebrain.
knowledge_points.plain: 脑分为后脑、中脑、前脑

knowledge_points.name: Hindbrain
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The hindbrain consists of structures located on top of the spinal cord. The hindbrain is our life support system; it controls the basic biological functions that keep us alive.
knowledge_points.plain: 维持生命基本功能的后脑

knowledge_points.name: Medulla
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The medulla is involved in the control of our blood pressure, heart rate, and breathing.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制血压、心率与呼吸

knowledge_points.name: Pons
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The pons (located just above the medulla and toward the front) connects the hindbrain with the midbrain and forebrain.
knowledge_points.plain: 连接后脑与中脑、前脑

knowledge_points.name: Cerebellum
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The cerebellum coordinates some habitual muscle movements, such as tracking a target with our eyes or moving our fingers when playing the saxophone.
knowledge_points.plain: 协调习惯性肌肉运动

knowledge_points.name: Midbrain
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In general, your midbrain coordinates simple movements with sensory information.
knowledge_points.plain: 整合感觉信息与简单运动

knowledge_points.name: Reticular formation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One specific structure in the midbrain you should be familiar with is the reticular formation. It is a netlike collection of cells throughout the midbrain that controls general body arousal and the ability to focus our attention.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制觉醒与注意力的网络

knowledge_points.name: Forebrain
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Areas of the forebrain control what we think of as thought and reason.
knowledge_points.plain: 负责思维与推理的脑区

knowledge_points.name: Thalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The thalamus is located on top of the brain stem. It is responsible for receiving the sensory signals coming up the spinal cord and sending them to the appropriate areas in the rest of the forebrain.
knowledge_points.plain: 中转上行感觉信号

knowledge_points.name: Hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The hypothalamus controls several metabolic functions, including body temperature, sexual arousal (libido), hunger, thirst, and the endocrine system.
knowledge_points.plain: 调节体温、饥饿与内分泌

knowledge_points.name: Amygdala and hippocampus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The amygdala is vital to our experiences of emotion, and the hippocampus is vital to our memory system.
knowledge_points.plain: 杏仁核管情绪，海马管记忆

knowledge_points.name: Limbic system
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These parts of the brain (thalamus, hypothalamus, amygdala, and hippocampus) are grouped together and called the limbic system because they all deal with aspects of emotion and memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 与情绪和记忆相关的脑区组合

knowledge_points.name: Cerebral cortex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When most people think of the human brain, they think of and picture the cerebral cortex. The gray, wrinkled surface of the brain is actually a thin (0.039-inch [1 mm]) layer of densely packed neurons.
knowledge_points.plain: 覆盖大脑的灰色薄层神经元

knowledge_points.name: Pruning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This process, called pruning, forms the complex neural web you now have in your brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 修剪神经连接、形成网络

knowledge_points.name: Hemispheres
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The cerebral cortex is divided into two hemispheres: left and right.
knowledge_points.plain: 大脑皮层分左右两半球

knowledge_points.name: Contralateral hemispheric organization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: (The idea that each side of the brain controls the opposite side of the body is called contralateral hemispheric organization.)
knowledge_points.plain: 一侧脑控制对侧身体

knowledge_points.name: Hemispheric specialization (brain lateralization)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This specialization of function in each hemisphere is called hemispheric specialization, or brain lateralization.
knowledge_points.plain: 两半球功能分工不同

knowledge_points.name: Split-brain patients
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Most of this research in differences between the hemispheres is done by examining split- brain patients—patients whose corpus callosum (the nerve bundle that connects the two hemispheres, see Figure 4.3) has been cut to treat severe epilepsy.
knowledge_points.researchers: Roger Sperry和Michael Gazzaniga的裂脑研究
knowledge_points.plain: 胼胝体被切断的患者

knowledge_points.name: Association area
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Any area of the cerebral cortex that is not associated with receiving sensory information or controlling muscle movements is labeled as an association area.
knowledge_points.plain: 未直接负责感觉或运动的皮层

knowledge_points.name: Frontal lobes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The frontal lobes are large areas of the cerebral cortex located at the top front part of the brain behind the eyes (see Figure 4.4).
knowledge_points.plain: 位于大脑前部的皮层区

knowledge_points.name: Prefrontal cortex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The anterior or front of the frontal lobe is called the prefrontal cortex and is thought to play a critical role in directing thought processes.
knowledge_points.plain: 负责计划、目标与情绪控制

knowledge_points.name: Broca’s area
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Broca’s area (named for Paul Broca, 1824–1880) is in the frontal lobe and is responsible for controlling the muscles involved in producing speech.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制说话肌肉运动的脑区

knowledge_points.name: Motor cortex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A thin vertical strip at the back of the frontal lobe (farthest from the eyes, see Figure 4.4) is called the motor cortex. This part of the cerebral cortex sends signals to our muscles, controlling our voluntary movements.
knowledge_points.plain: 发出随意运动指令

knowledge_points.name: Parietal lobes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The parietal lobes are located behind the frontal lobe but still on the top of the brain (see Figure 4.4).
knowledge_points.plain: 位于额叶后方的顶部皮层

knowledge_points.name: Somatosensory cortex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The parietal lobes contain the somatosensory cortex (also known as the sensory cortex), which is located right behind the motor cortex in the frontal lobe.
knowledge_points.plain: 接收身体触觉信息

knowledge_points.name: Phantom limb syndrome
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One fascinating phenomenon that involves the somatosensory cortex is phantom limb syndrome: if an individual loses a part of their body, like an arm or hand, the person may still perceive sensations from that lost limb because part of their somatosensory cortex is still “mapped” to the missing body part.
knowledge_points.plain: 失去肢体后仍感到其存在

knowledge_points.name: Occipital lobes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our occipital lobes are at the very back of our brain, farthest from our eyes. This is somewhat counterintuitive since one of the major functions of this lobe is to interpret messages from our eyes in our visual cortex.
knowledge_points.plain: 位于脑后、处理视觉

knowledge_points.name: Temporal lobes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The temporal lobes process sound sensed by our ears.
knowledge_points.plain: 处理听觉信息

knowledge_points.name: Wernicke’s area
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Wernicke’s area is involved with linguistic processing via both written and spoken speech.
knowledge_points.plain: 负责语言理解的脑区

knowledge_points.name: Brain plasticity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researchers know some of the functions of different areas of the cerebral cortex, but they have also discovered that the brain is somewhat plastic or flexible.
knowledge_points.plain: 大脑可重组以适应损伤

knowledge_points.name: Consciousness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: While you are reading this text, you can probably become aware of your sense of consciousness.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自身心理状态的觉察

knowledge_points.name: Mere exposure effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The mere exposure effect (see also Unit 4) occurs when we prefer stimuli we have seen before over novel stimuli, even if we do not consciously remember seeing the old stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 偏好曾见过的刺激

knowledge_points.name: Priming
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A closely related concept is priming. Research participants respond more quickly and/or accurately to questions they have seen before, even if they do not remember seeing them.
knowledge_points.plain: 先前经历加快后续反应

knowledge_points.name: Blind sight
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another fascinating phenomenon that demonstrates levels of consciousness is blind sight. Some people who report being blind can nonetheless accurately describe the path of a moving object or accurately grasp objects they say they cannot see!
knowledge_points.plain: 盲人仍能准确感知物体

knowledge_points.name: Conscious level
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The information about yourself and your environment you are currently aware of.
knowledge_points.plain: 当前意识到的信息

knowledge_points.name: Nonconscious level
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Body processes controlled by your mind that we are not usually (or ever) aware of.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制心跳等不自觉过程

knowledge_points.name: Preconscious level
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Information about yourself or your environment that you are not currently thinking about (not in your conscious level) but you could be.
knowledge_points.plain: 可随时调入意识的信息

knowledge_points.name: Subconscious level
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Information that we are not consciously aware of but we know must exist due to behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 未觉察但影响行为的信息

knowledge_points.name: Unconscious level
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic psychologists believe some events and feelings are unacceptable to our conscious mind and are repressed into the unconscious mind.
knowledge_points.plain: 被压抑、难以觉察的内容

knowledge_points.name: Psychoactive drugs
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychoactive drugs are chemicals that change the chemistry of the brain (and the rest of the body) and induce an altered state of consciousness.
knowledge_points.plain: 改变脑化学、改变意识

knowledge_points.name: Blood-brain barrier
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Normally, the brain is protected from harmful chemicals in the bloodstream by thicker walls surrounding the brain’s blood vessels. This is called the blood-brain barrier.
knowledge_points.plain: 保护大脑免受血液有害物

knowledge_points.name: Agonists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The drugs that mimic neurotransmitters are called agonists. These drugs fit in the receptor sites on a neuron that normally receive the neurotransmitter and function as that neurotransmitter normally would.
knowledge_points.plain: 模拟神经递质作用的药物

knowledge_points.name: Antagonists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The drugs that block neurotransmitters are called antagonists. These molecules don't fit the receptor sites well enough to substitute for them but do fit well enough to occupy the same space, thereby preventing neurotransmitters or agonists from causing a reaction.
knowledge_points.plain: 阻断神经递质作用的药物

knowledge_points.name: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One example of this kind of drug is Prozac, which is called a “selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor” because it prevents serotonin from being reabsorbed back into the neuron.
knowledge_points.plain: 阻止血清素被回收的药物

knowledge_points.name: Tolerance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This change causes tolerance, a physiological change that produces a need for more of the same drug in order to achieve the same effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 需加大剂量才能达到原效果

knowledge_points.name: Withdrawal symptoms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Tolerance will eventually cause withdrawal symptoms in users. Withdrawal symptoms vary from drug to drug.
knowledge_points.plain: 停药后出现的不适反应

knowledge_points.name: Psychological dependence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Persons psychologically dependent on a drug feel an intense desire for the drug because they are convinced they need it in order to perform or feel a certain way.
knowledge_points.plain: 心理上强烈渴望该药物

knowledge_points.name: Physical dependence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Persons physically dependent on a substance have a tolerance for the drug, experience withdrawal symptoms without it, and need the drug to avoid the withdrawal symptoms.
knowledge_points.plain: 身体需要药物以避免戒断

knowledge_points.name: Stimulants
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Stimulants speed up body processes, including autonomic nervous system functions such as heart and respiration rates.
knowledge_points.plain: 加快身体机能与心率

knowledge_points.name: Depressants
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Depressants slow down the same body systems that stimulants speed up.
knowledge_points.plain: 减慢身体机能活动

knowledge_points.name: Hallucinogens
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Hallucinogens (also sometimes called psychedelics) do not necessarily speed up or slow down the body. These drugs cause changes in perceptions of reality, including sensory hallucinations, loss of identity, and vivid fantasies.
knowledge_points.plain: 引起感知与幻觉改变

knowledge_points.name: Reverse tolerance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This effect is sometimes called reverse tolerance because the second dose may be less than the first but cause the same or greater effects.
knowledge_points.plain: 小剂量也产生更强效果

knowledge_points.name: Opiates
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The opiates all act as agonists for endorphins and thus are powerful painkillers and mood elevators.
knowledge_points.plain: 类似内啡肽的强效止痛药

knowledge_points.name: Sleep deprived
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Many studies show that a large percentage of high school and college students are sleep deprived, meaning they do not get as much sleep as their body wants.
knowledge_points.plain: 睡眠不足、未满足身体需要

knowledge_points.name: Circadian rhythm
knowledge_points.definition_quote: You may be familiar with the term circadian rhythm. During a 24- hour day, our metabolic and thought processes follow a certain pattern.
knowledge_points.plain: 约24小时的生理节律

knowledge_points.name: Sleep cycle
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our sleep cycle is our typical pattern of sleep.
knowledge_points.plain: 睡眠的典型阶段模式

knowledge_points.name: Sleep onset
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The period when we are falling asleep is called sleep onset.
knowledge_points.plain: 从清醒到入睡的过渡期

knowledge_points.name: Alpha waves
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our brain produces alpha waves when we are drowsy but awake.
knowledge_points.plain: 困倦清醒时的脑电波

knowledge_points.name: Theta waves
knowledge_points.definition_quote: While we are awake and in stages NREM 1 and NREM 2, our brains produce theta waves, which are relatively high-frequency, low-amplitude waves.
knowledge_points.plain: NREM一期和二期的脑波

knowledge_points.name: Sleep spindles
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In NREM stage 2, the EEG starts to show sleep spindles, which are short bursts of rapid brain waves.
knowledge_points.plain: NREM二期的快速脑波爆发

knowledge_points.name: Delta sleep
knowledge_points.definition_quote: From there, we move into NREM stage 3, which is sometimes called delta sleep (also called deep or slow- wave sleep) because of the delta waves that exist during these stages.
knowledge_points.plain: 深睡期、以慢波为主

knowledge_points.name: Restoration of resources
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This finding indicates that one of the functions of sleep (and the different stages in the sleep cycle) is restoration of resources: sleep is necessary because our body has to rebuild various resources it used while we were awake and active.
knowledge_points.plain: 睡眠重建白天消耗的资源

knowledge_points.name: REM sleep
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This is REM—rapid eye movement. This sleep stage is sometimes called paradoxical sleep since our brain waves appear as active and intense as they do when we are awake.
knowledge_points.plain: 快速眼动、脑波活跃的睡眠

knowledge_points.name: REM rebound
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Individuals deprived of REM sleep will experience REM rebound—experiencing more and longer periods of REM—the next time they are allowed to sleep normally.
knowledge_points.plain: 缺REM后补回更多REM

knowledge_points.name: Insomnia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Insomnia is far and away the most common sleep disorder, affecting up to 10 percent of the population. An insomniac has persistent problems getting to sleep or staying asleep at night.
knowledge_points.plain: 持续难以入睡或维持睡眠

knowledge_points.name: Narcolepsy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Narcolepsy occurs far more rarely than insomnia, occurring in less than 0.001 percent of the population. Narcoleptics suffer from periods of intense sleepiness and may fall asleep at unpredictable and inappropriate times.
knowledge_points.plain: 白天突然不可控地入睡

knowledge_points.name: Sleep apnea
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sleep apnea may be almost as common as insomnia and, in some ways, might be more serious. Apnea causes a person to stop breathing for short periods of time during the night.
knowledge_points.plain: 夜间呼吸短暂停止

knowledge_points.name: Night terrors
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Night terrors usually affect young children, and most do not remember the episode when they wake up.
knowledge_points.plain: 儿童夜间惊醒且不记得

knowledge_points.name: Somnambulism (sleepwalking)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The exact causes are not known, but night terrors are probably related in some way to somnambulism (sleepwalking).
knowledge_points.plain: 睡眠中行走

knowledge_points.name: Dreams
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Dreams are the series of storylike images we experience as we sleep.
knowledge_points.plain: 睡眠中经历的故事性影像

knowledge_points.name: Lucid dreams
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some of us even report lucid dreams in which we are aware that we are dreaming and can control the storyline of the dream.
knowledge_points.plain: 知道自己在做梦并能控制

knowledge_points.name: Activation-synthesis theory of dreaming
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The activation-synthesis theory of dreaming looks at dreams first as biological phenomena. Brain imaging proves that our brain is very active during REM sleep. This theory proposes that perhaps dreams are nothing more than the brain’s interpretations of what is happening physiologically during REM sleep.
knowledge_points.plain: 梦是对REM期生理活动的解释

knowledge_points.name: Information-processing theory of dreaming
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The information-processing theory of dreaming suggests that we use dreams to process the events of the day.
knowledge_points.plain: 用梦加工白天的事件

knowledge_points.name: Consolidation theory of dreams
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The information-processing theory of dreaming is closely related to the consolidation theory of dreams: one of the functions of dreams might be to help us encode events and information in our short-term memory into our long-term memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 梦帮助记忆巩固

knowledge_points.name: Sensation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: sensation in more general terms: the activation of our senses (eyes, ears, and so on)
knowledge_points.plain: 感官被激活的过程

knowledge_points.name: Perception
knowledge_points.definition_quote: perception as the process of understanding these sensations
knowledge_points.plain: 理解感觉信息的过程

knowledge_points.name: Transduction
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These messages go through a process called transduction, which means the signals are transformed into neural impulses.
knowledge_points.plain: 刺激转化为神经冲动

knowledge_points.name: Sensory adaptation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: sensory adaptation (decreasing responsiveness to stimuli due to constant stimulation)
knowledge_points.plain: 持续刺激导致反应减弱

knowledge_points.name: Sensory habituation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: sensory habituation (our perception of sensations is partially due to how focused we are on them)
knowledge_points.plain: 注意力集中影响感觉

knowledge_points.name: Cocktail party effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you are talking with a friend and someone across the room says your name, your attention will probably involuntarily switch across the room. (This is sometimes called the cocktail party effect.)
knowledge_points.plain: 无意中注意到自己名字

knowledge_points.name: Synesthesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One example is synesthesia, a phenomenon some people experience in which the activation of one sense, like seeing a color, activates another sense, like hearing a specific sound (or vice versa)!
knowledge_points.plain: 一种感觉引发另一种感觉

knowledge_points.name: Prosopagnosia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Prosopagnosia, another rare condition, involves the inability to recognize faces.
knowledge_points.plain: 无法辨认人脸

knowledge_points.name: Vision
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Vision is the dominant sense in human beings.
knowledge_points.plain: 人类最主要的感觉

knowledge_points.name: Retina
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The focused inverted image projects on the retina, which is like a screen on the back of your eye.
knowledge_points.plain: 眼球后部成像的屏幕

knowledge_points.name: Hues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Different wavelengths within the visible light spectrum appear as different hues.
knowledge_points.plain: 不同波长对应不同色调

knowledge_points.name: Amplitude
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another important factor is the wave’s amplitude (height), which dictates its intensity.
knowledge_points.plain: 波的振幅决定颜色强度

knowledge_points.name: Cornea
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The reflected light first enters the eye through the cornea.
knowledge_points.plain: 保护眼球并帮助聚焦

knowledge_points.name: Pupil
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The pupil is like the shutter of a camera.
knowledge_points.plain: 控制进光量的开口

knowledge_points.name: Accommodation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Through a process called accommodation, light that enters the pupil is focused by the lens; the lens is curved and flexible so it can change shape to focus the light on the retina.
knowledge_points.plain: 晶状体改变形状以聚焦

knowledge_points.name: Transduction
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The term transduction refers to the translation of incoming stimuli into neural signals.
knowledge_points.plain: 刺激转换为神经信号

knowledge_points.name: Cones
knowledge_points.definition_quote: cones, which are cells that are activated by color
knowledge_points.plain: 感受颜色的视锥细胞

knowledge_points.name: Rods
knowledge_points.definition_quote: rods, which are cells that respond to black and white
knowledge_points.plain: 感受明暗的视杆细胞

knowledge_points.name: Fovea
knowledge_points.definition_quote: At the very center of the retina is an indentation called the fovea that contains the highest concentration of cones.
knowledge_points.plain: 视网膜中央、视锥最密集

knowledge_points.name: Blind spot
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The spot where the optic nerve leaves the retina has no rods or cones, so it is referred to as the blind spot.
knowledge_points.plain: 视神经出口、无感光细胞

knowledge_points.name: Optic chiasm
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The spot where the nerves cross each other is called the optic chiasm.
knowledge_points.plain: 视神经交叉处

knowledge_points.name: Feature detectors
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The visual cortex has feature detectors for vertical lines, curves, motion, and many other features of images.
knowledge_points.plain: 对特定视觉特征反应的神经元

knowledge_points.name: Theories of color vision
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Competing theories exist about how and why we see color.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释颜色知觉的不同理论

knowledge_points.name: Trichromatic theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The oldest and simplest theory is trichromatic theory. This theory hypothesizes that we have three types of cones in the retina and that each type detects a different primary color of light: blue, red, or green.
knowledge_points.plain: 三种视锥感受红绿蓝

knowledge_points.name: Afterimage
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you stare at one color for a while and then look at a white or blank space, you will see a negative color afterimage.
knowledge_points.plain: 注视后看到的互补色残像

knowledge_points.name: Dichromatism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Individuals with dichromatism cannot see either red/green shades or blue/yellow shades.
knowledge_points.plain: 红绿或蓝黄辨色困难

knowledge_points.name: Opponent-process theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The opponent-process theory states that the sensory receptors arranged in the retina come in pairs: red/green pairs, yellow/blue pairs, and black/white pairs.
knowledge_points.plain: 颜色感受器成对相互抑制

knowledge_points.name: Pitch
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Frequency refers to the length of the waves and determines pitch, which is measured in megahertz.
knowledge_points.plain: 声波频率决定音高

knowledge_points.name: Loudness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Amplitude is the height of the wave and determines the loudness of the sound, which is measured in decibels.
knowledge_points.plain: 声波振幅决定响度

knowledge_points.name: Cochlea
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The oval window membrane is attached to the cochlea, a structure shaped like a snail’s shell and filled with fluid.
knowledge_points.plain: 内耳蜗形、充满液体的结构

knowledge_points.name: Sound localization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In this way, we can determine approximately where a sound originated; this is called sound localization.
knowledge_points.plain: 判断声音来源方向

knowledge_points.name: Pitch theories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As with color vision, two different theories describe the two processes involved in hearing pitch: place theory and frequency theory.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释音高感知的两种理论

knowledge_points.name: Place theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Place theory holds that the hair cells in the cochlea respond to different frequencies of sound based on where they are located in the cochlea.
knowledge_points.plain: 不同位置毛细胞感受不同频率

knowledge_points.name: Frequency theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Frequency theory states that we sense pitch because the hair cells fire at different rates (frequencies) in the cochlea.
knowledge_points.plain: 毛细胞放电频率决定音高

knowledge_points.name: Conduction deafness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Conduction deafness occurs when something goes wrong with the system of conducting the sound to the cochlea (in the ear canal, eardrum, hammer/anvil/stirrup, or oval window).
knowledge_points.plain: 声音传导通路出问题

knowledge_points.name: Nerve deafness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Nerve deafness (or sensorineural deafness) occurs when the hair cells in the cochlea are damaged, usually by loud noise.
knowledge_points.plain: 耳蜗毛细胞受损致聋

knowledge_points.name: Gate control theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Gate control theory helps explain how we experience pain the way we do. This theory explains that some pain messages have a higher priority than others.
knowledge_points.plain: 高强度疼痛信息优先传递

knowledge_points.name: Pain receptors
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If touch or temperature receptors are stimulated sharply, a different kind of nerve ending called pain receptors will also fire.
knowledge_points.plain: 受到强烈刺激时产生痛觉

knowledge_points.name: Endorphins
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Endorphins, or pain-killing chemicals in the body, also swing the gate shut.
knowledge_points.plain: 体内天然止痛化学物质

knowledge_points.name: Taste buds
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Chemicals from the food we eat (or whatever else we stick into our mouths) are absorbed by taste buds on our tongue (see Figure 6.3).
knowledge_points.plain: 舌上感受味道的结构

knowledge_points.name: Papillae
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Taste receptors are located on papillae, which are the bumps you can see on your tongue.
knowledge_points.plain: 舌面可见的小突起

knowledge_points.name: Five different types of tastes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Humans sense five different types of tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami (savory or meaty taste), and oleogutus (taste of fat).
knowledge_points.plain: 甜、咸、酸、苦、鲜、脂肪味

knowledge_points.name: Supertasters
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If all the bumps are packed tightly together, you probably taste food intensely. (These individuals are called supertasters.)
knowledge_points.plain: 味蕾密集、味觉强烈的人

knowledge_points.name: Smell (or Olfaction)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our sense of smell also depends on chemicals emitted by substances.
knowledge_points.plain: 依赖化学分子的嗅觉

knowledge_points.name: Olfactory bulb
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These receptor cells are linked to the olfactory bulb (see Figure 6.4), which gathers the messages from the olfactory receptor cells and sends this information to the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 收集嗅觉信息并传向大脑

knowledge_points.name: Vestibular sense
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our vestibular sense tells us about how our body is oriented in space.
knowledge_points.plain: 感知身体在空间中的朝向

knowledge_points.name: Semicircular canals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Three semicircular canals in the inner ear (see Figure 6.2) give the brain feedback about body orientation.
knowledge_points.plain: 内耳中感受头部转动的管道

knowledge_points.name: Kinesthetic sense (kinesthesis)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: While our vestibular sense keeps track of the overall orientation of our body, our kinesthetic sense (kinesthesis) gives us feedback about the position and orientation of specific body parts.
knowledge_points.plain: 感知各肢体位置与运动

knowledge_points.name: Perception
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Perception is the process of understanding and interpreting sensations.
knowledge_points.plain: 理解和解释感觉的过程

knowledge_points.name: Psychophysics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychophysics is the study of the interaction between the sensations we receive and our experience of them.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究感觉与主观体验的关系

knowledge_points.name: absolute threshold
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The absolute threshold is the smallest amount of stimulus we can detect.
knowledge_points.plain: 能觉察到的最小刺激量

knowledge_points.name: subliminal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Stimuli below our absolute threshold are said to be subliminal.
knowledge_points.plain: 低于绝对阈限的刺激

knowledge_points.name: difference threshold
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The difference threshold, sometimes called a just-noticeable difference, is the smallest amount of change needed in a stimulus before we detect a change.
knowledge_points.plain: 刚能觉察的刺激最小变化

knowledge_points.name: Weber’s law
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This threshold is computed by Weber’s law, which states that the change needed is proportional to the original intensity of the stimulus.
knowledge_points.plain: 变化量与原有刺激强度成正比

knowledge_points.name: signal detection theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Signal detection theory investigates the effects of the distractions and interference we experience while perceiving the world.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究干扰下如何觉察刺激

knowledge_points.name: false positive
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A false positive is when we think we perceive a stimulus that is not there.
knowledge_points.plain: 误以为存在实际没有的刺激

knowledge_points.name: false negative
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A false negative is not perceiving a stimulus that is present.
knowledge_points.plain: 未觉察到实际存在的刺激

knowledge_points.name: top-down processing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Top-down processing occurs when you use your background knowledge to fill in gaps in what you perceive.
knowledge_points.plain: 用背景知识补全所感知信息

knowledge_points.name: schemata
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our experience creates schemata (also called schema), which are mental representations of how we expect the world to be.
knowledge_points.plain: 对世界如何运作的心理表征

knowledge_points.name: perceptual set
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Schemata can create a perceptual set, which is a predisposition to perceiving something in a certain way.
knowledge_points.plain: 以特定方式感知事物的倾向

knowledge_points.name: bottom-up processing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Instead of using our experience to perceive an object, we use only the features of the object itself to build a complete perception.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据刺激本身特征构建知觉

knowledge_points.name: figure-ground relationship
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the first perceptual decisions our mind must make is the figure-ground relationship. What part of a visual image is the figure and what part is the ground or background?
knowledge_points.plain: 区分图形与背景的知觉关系

knowledge_points.name: Gestalt psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Gestalt psychology points out that we normally perceive images as groups, not as isolated elements.
knowledge_points.plain: 强调整体组织而非孤立元素

knowledge_points.name: Proximity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that are close together are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group.
knowledge_points.plain: 邻近的物体易归为一组

knowledge_points.name: Similarity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that are similar in appearance are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group.
knowledge_points.plain: 相似的物体易归为一组

knowledge_points.name: Continuity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that are arranged in a continuous line or curve (such as a trail or a geometric figure) are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group.
knowledge_points.plain: 连续线条或曲线易归为一组

knowledge_points.name: Closure
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects that make up a recognizable image are more likely to be perceived as belonging in the same group even if the image contains gaps that the mind needs to fill in; note that this perception is influenced by top-down processing.
knowledge_points.plain: 补全缺口以看成完整图形

knowledge_points.name: constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our ability to maintain a constant perception of an object despite these changes is called constancy.
knowledge_points.plain: 随条件变化仍保持知觉恒定

knowledge_points.name: size constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We keep a constant size in mind for an object (if we are familiar with the typical size of the object) and know that it does not grow or shrink in size as it moves closer or farther away.
knowledge_points.plain: 随距离变化仍知物体大小不变

knowledge_points.name: shape constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Objects viewed from different angles produce different shapes on our retinas, but we know the shape of an object remains constant.
knowledge_points.plain: 视角变化仍知物体形状不变

knowledge_points.name: brightness constancy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We perceive objects as being a constant color even as the light reflecting off the object changes.
knowledge_points.plain: 光照变化仍知物体颜色不变

knowledge_points.name: stroboscopic effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A common example of this is the stroboscopic effect, used in movies or flip books. Images in a series of still pictures presented at a certain speed will appear to be moving.
knowledge_points.plain: 连续静止画面看起来在运动

knowledge_points.name: phi phenomenon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another example you have probably encountered on movie marquees and with holiday lights is the phi phenomenon. A series of lightbulbs turned on and off at a particular rate will appear to be one moving light.
knowledge_points.plain: 灯光依次明灭看似一个光点在动

knowledge_points.name: autokinetic effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A third example is the autokinetic effect. If a spot of light is projected steadily onto the same place on a wall of an otherwise dark room and people are asked to stare at it, they will report seeing it move.
knowledge_points.plain: 暗室固定光点看似移动

knowledge_points.name: depth perception
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Without depth perception, we would perceive the world as a two-dimensional flat surface and be unable to differentiate between what is near and what is far.
knowledge_points.plain: 判断远近和三维空间的能力

knowledge_points.name: visual cliff
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researcher Eleanor Gibson used the visual cliff experiment to determine when human infants can perceive depth. An infant is placed onto one side of a glass-topped table that creates the impression of a cliff.
knowledge_points.plain: 制造悬崖错觉的玻璃台实验

knowledge_points.name: monocular depth cues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: monocular depth cues (depth cues that do not depend on having two eyes)
knowledge_points.plain: 不需双眼参与的深度线索

knowledge_points.name: linear perspective
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the most common cues is linear perspective. If you wanted to draw a railroad track that runs away from the viewer off into the distance, most likely you would start by drawing two lines that converge somewhere toward the top of your paper.
knowledge_points.plain: 平行线汇聚表现纵深感

knowledge_points.name: relative size
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you added a drawing of the train, you might use the relative size cue. You would draw the boxcars closer to the viewer as larger than the engine off in the distance.
knowledge_points.plain: 近大远小判断物体远近

knowledge_points.name: interposition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A water tower blocking our view of part of the train would be seen as closer to us due to the interposition cue; objects that block the view to other objects must be closer to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 被遮挡物显得更远

knowledge_points.name: texture gradient
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This cue is called texture gradient; we know that we can see details in texture close to us but not far away.
knowledge_points.plain: 近处纹理清晰远处模糊

knowledge_points.name: shadowing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: By shading part of your picture, you can imply where the light source is and thus imply depth and position of objects.
knowledge_points.plain: 用阴影暗示光源和深度

knowledge_points.name: binocular depth cues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: binocular depth cues (cues that depend on having two eyes)
knowledge_points.plain: 依赖双眼的深度线索

knowledge_points.name: retinal disparity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Each of our eyes will view an object from a slightly different angle. The brain receives both images. It knows that if the object is far away, the images will be similar, but the closer the object is, the more disparity there will be between the images coming from each eye.
knowledge_points.plain: 双眼图像差异提供深度信息

knowledge_points.name: convergence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The other binocular depth cue is convergence. As an object gets closer to our face, our eyes must move toward each other to keep focused on the object.
knowledge_points.plain: 物体靠近时双眼向内会聚

knowledge_points.name: perceptual sets
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cross- cultural research demonstrates that some basic perceptual sets are learned from our culture.
knowledge_points.plain: 部分知觉定势由文化习得

knowledge_points.name: Muller-Lyer illusion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Line A should look longer even though both lines are actually the same length.
knowledge_points.plain: 等长线段看起来长度不同

knowledge_points.name: noncarpentered cultures
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People who come from noncarpentered cultures that do not often use right angles and corners in their building and architecture are not usually fooled by the Muller-Lyer illusion.
knowledge_points.plain: 不常用直角的建筑文化

knowledge_points.name: extrasensory perception (ESP)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: someone claiming to have “extrasensory perception” is claiming to perceive a sensation “outside” the senses discussed in Unit 1.
knowledge_points.plain: 声称感知感官之外的信息

knowledge_points.name: thinking and creativity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Describing thinking and creativity is one of the most challenging areas in the science of psychology.
knowledge_points.plain: 思维与创造力难以描述定义

knowledge_points.name: concepts
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We each have cognitive rules we apply to stimuli from our environment that allow us to categorize and think about the objects, people, and ideas we encounter.
knowledge_points.plain: 用于归类思考的心理规则

knowledge_points.name: prototypes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We may base our concepts on prototypes, or what we think is the most typical example of a particular concept.
knowledge_points.plain: 概念中最典型的例子

knowledge_points.name: images
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another type of thought, images, are the mental pictures we create in our minds of the outside world.
knowledge_points.plain: 头脑中对外界形成的心理图像

knowledge_points.name: algorithm
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An algorithm is a rule that guarantees the right solution by using a formula or other foolproof method.
knowledge_points.plain: 保证正确解的公式化方法

knowledge_points.name: heuristic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A heuristic is a rule of thumb—a strategy we can use to make a quick but not necessarily accurate judgment in a situation.
knowledge_points.plain: 快速但不一定准确的判断策略

knowledge_points.name: availability heuristic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Judging a situation based on examples of similar situations that come to mind initially.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据易想起的例子判断

knowledge_points.name: representativeness heuristic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Judging a situation based on how similar the aspects are to prototypes the person holds in his or her mind.
knowledge_points.plain: 依据与原型相似度判断

knowledge_points.name: overconfidence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Overconfidence is our tendency to overestimate how accurate our judgments are.
knowledge_points.plain: 高估自己判断的准确性

knowledge_points.name: belief bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Belief bias occurs when we make illogical conclusions to confirm our preexisting beliefs.
knowledge_points.plain: 为维护原信念而错误推理

knowledge_points.name: belief perseverance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Belief perseverance refers to our tendency to maintain a belief even after the evidence we used to form the belief is contradicted.
knowledge_points.plain: 证据被推翻后仍坚持信念

knowledge_points.name: gambler’s fallacy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another example of a limitation of a heuristic is the gambler’s fallacy: this occurs when we believe that a certain event or outcome is more or less likely to occur because of how often it has recently occurred.
knowledge_points.plain: 误以为近期结果改变下次概率

knowledge_points.name: sunk-cost fallacy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The sunk-cost fallacy can also influence our thinking in negative ways. Sometimes we are unwilling to change a course of action because we spent a lot of effort and time trying to make that solution work, even when it becomes clear that the course of action is unlikely to solve the problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 因已投入而不愿改变方案

knowledge_points.name: mental set
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Mental set (also called rigidity) refers to the tendency to fall into established thought patterns.
knowledge_points.plain: 固守既有思路解决问题

knowledge_points.name: functional fixedness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One specific example of rigidity is functional fixedness, the inability to see a new use for an object.
knowledge_points.plain: 看不到物体的新用途

knowledge_points.name: subgoals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies show that good problem solvers identify subgoals, which are smaller and more manageable problems they need to solve in order to solve the whole problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 把总问题拆成的较小问题

knowledge_points.name: confirmation bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another obstacle to successful problem-solving is confirmation bias. Many studies show that we tend to look for evidence that confirms our beliefs and ignore evidence that contradicts what we think is true.
knowledge_points.plain: 只找支持自身信念的证据

knowledge_points.name: framing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Framing refers to the idea that the same information can be presented in different ways and the method of presentation can drastically change the way we view a problem or an issue.
knowledge_points.plain: 表述方式影响问题判断

knowledge_points.name: convergent thinking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: convergent thinking, which is thinking pointed toward one solution
knowledge_points.plain: 指向单一解决方案的思维

knowledge_points.name: divergent thinking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: divergent thinking, which is thinking that searches for multiple possible answers to a question.
knowledge_points.plain: 寻求多个可能答案的思维

knowledge_points.name: models, or explanations, of how memory works
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Several different models, or explanations, of how memory works have emerged from memory research.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释记忆运作的不同模型

knowledge_points.name: three-box/information-processing model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The principal model of memory is the three-box model, also called the information-processing model or the multi-store model. This model proposes the three stages that information passes through before it is stored (see Figure 9.1).
knowledge_points.plain: 信息经三阶段存储的记忆模型

knowledge_points.name: sensory memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The first stop for external events is sensory memory. It is a holding tank for incoming sensory information.
knowledge_points.plain: 暂存外来感觉信息的容器

knowledge_points.name: iconic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: less than a second for visual information (iconic memory)
knowledge_points.plain: 视觉信息的极短暂感觉记忆

knowledge_points.name: echoic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: three to four seconds for auditory information (echoic memory)
knowledge_points.plain: 听觉信息约持续数秒

knowledge_points.name: selective attention
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We encode what we are attending to or what is important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 选择编码重要或关注的信息

knowledge_points.name: cocktail party effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, once a sensory message that you knew was important (like someone saying your name or hearing someone shout “Fire!”) entered sensory memory, you switched your attention to that message, and it was encoded into your short-term memory. (This phenomenon is called the cocktail party effect.)
knowledge_points.plain: 重要声音会吸引注意并被编码

knowledge_points.name: inattentional blindness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We’ve all experienced inattentional blindness: when we fail to perceive something that was in our visual field (and that our eyes probably sensed) because we weren’t paying attention to it and were intensely focused on something else.
knowledge_points.plain: 专注时看不见视野内事物

knowledge_points.name: change blindness
