knowledge_points.definition_quote: A closely related experience is change blindness: sometimes we do not observe an obvious change in our visual world because we are selectively attending to something else and do not perceive that an object or person changed.
knowledge_points.plain: 未注意到视觉场景的明显变化

knowledge_points.name: short-term memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Everything you are thinking at the current moment is held in your short-term memory, and if you are trying to do something with that information, it’s in your working memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 当前正在思考的信息的暂时存储

knowledge_points.name: working memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Working memory is your ability to manipulate items in your short-term memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 操作短时记忆内容的能力

knowledge_points.name: central executive
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The central executive—monitors incoming information and determines what other systems should be involved in processing the information.
knowledge_points.plain: 监控信息并分配加工系统

knowledge_points.name: visuospatial sketchpad
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The visuospatial sketchpad—deals with visual information; this is our “mind’s eye” that we use to visualize the world.
knowledge_points.plain: 处理视觉空间信息的心理画板

knowledge_points.name: auditory loop
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The auditory loop—deals with words or numbers.
knowledge_points.plain: 处理词语或数字的语音回路

knowledge_points.name: maintenance rehearsal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When you get a confirmation code, you probably need to repeat it to yourself until you type it in; this is an example of maintenance rehearsal.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过重复把信息保持在短时记忆

knowledge_points.name: elaborative rehearsal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Elaborative rehearsal is a type of effortful processing: it occurs when we focus on putting mental effort into encoding the meaning of a term, an event, a process, and so on.
knowledge_points.plain: 努力加工信息意义以助编码

knowledge_points.name: semantic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This is closely related to semantic memory, which involves memories related to the significance or meaning of information.
knowledge_points.plain: 关于信息意义的记忆

knowledge_points.name: long-term memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Long-term memory is our permanent storage.
knowledge_points.plain: 永久保存信息的记忆系统

knowledge_points.name: episodic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Memories of specific events, stored in a sequential series of events.
knowledge_points.plain: 按顺序储存的具体事件记忆

knowledge_points.name: semantic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: General knowledge of the world, stored as facts, meanings, or categories rather than sequentially.
knowledge_points.plain: 储存事实意义和类别知识

knowledge_points.name: procedural memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Memories of skills and how to perform them.
knowledge_points.plain: 关于技能如何操作的记忆

knowledge_points.name: explicit memories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Explicit memories (also called declarative memories) are what we usually think of first. They are the conscious memories of facts or events we actively tried to remember.
knowledge_points.plain: 主动回忆事实或事件的意识记忆

knowledge_points.name: implicit memories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Implicit memories (also called nondeclarative memories) are unintentional memories that we might not even realize we have.
knowledge_points.plain: 无意形成且未意识到的记忆

knowledge_points.name: prospective memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Yet another type of memory is prospective memory, which is your memory for things you plan to do in the future.
knowledge_points.plain: 记住未来要做的事情

knowledge_points.name: eidetic memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Luria and other researchers showed that these rare individuals seem to use very powerful and enduring visual images.
knowledge_points.plain: 极少数人具有的逼真持久视觉记忆

knowledge_points.name: levels of processing model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An alternate way to think about memory is the levels of processing model. This theory explains why we remember what we do by examining how deeply the memory was processed or thought about.
knowledge_points.plain: 按加工深度解释记忆的模型

knowledge_points.name: shallowly encoded
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you simply repeat a fact to yourself several times and then write it on your test as quickly as you can, you have only shallowly encoded that fact and you will forget it quickly.
knowledge_points.plain: 只机械重复而浅层加工

knowledge_points.name: deeply encoded
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, if you study the context and research the reasons behind the fact, you have deeply encoded it and will likely recall it later.
knowledge_points.plain: 结合语境和意义深入加工

knowledge_points.name: long-term potentiation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: At the neurological level, researchers focus on a process called long-term potentiation. Studies show that neurons can strengthen connections between each other.
knowledge_points.plain: 重复激活增强神经元连接

knowledge_points.name: encoding
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Encoding is the process by which we put information into our memories, and it can be affected by many factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 把信息放入记忆的过程

knowledge_points.name: primacy effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The primacy effect predicts that we are more likely to recall items presented at the beginning of a list.
knowledge_points.plain: 更易记住列表开头项目

knowledge_points.name: recency effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The recency effect is demonstrated by our ability to recall the items at the end of a list.
knowledge_points.plain: 更易记住列表末尾项目

knowledge_points.name: serial position effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Together the primacy effect and recency effect demonstrate the serial position effect (also called the serial position curve). This effect is seen when recall of a list is affected by the order of items in a list.
knowledge_points.plain: 回忆受项目在列表中位置影响

knowledge_points.name: method of loci
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A well-known example is the method of loci. This method involves using imagery to associate the things you want to remember with various places.
knowledge_points.plain: 用地点意象关联待记内容

knowledge_points.name: spacing effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the most robust findings in memory research is called the spacing effect. Research has consistently demonstrated the benefit of spacing studying out or using what is called distributed practice, as opposed to massed practice.
knowledge_points.plain: 分散学习优于集中学习

knowledge_points.name: chunking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, this limit can be expanded through a process called chunking. If you want to remember a grocery list with 15 items on it, you should chunk, or group, the items into no more than seven groups.
knowledge_points.plain: 把多个项目分组以便记忆

knowledge_points.name: mnemonic devices
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Most mnemonic devices, which are memory aids, are really examples of chunking.
knowledge_points.plain: 借分组等技巧辅助记忆

knowledge_points.name: hippocampus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: By studying patients with specific brain damage, we know that the hippocampus is important in encoding new memories.
knowledge_points.plain: 负责编码新记忆的脑结构

knowledge_points.name: anterograde amnesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Individuals with damage to the hippocampus might have anterograde amnesia (cannot encode new memories) but can recall events already in memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 无法形成新的记忆

knowledge_points.name: retrograde amnesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with retrograde amnesia have a different problem; they are unable to remember information learned before a trauma to the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 不能回忆创伤前经历

knowledge_points.name: cerebellum
knowledge_points.definition_quote: (Studies on animals indicate that procedural memories are stored in the cerebellum.)
knowledge_points.plain: 储存程序性记忆的脑结构

knowledge_points.name: retrieval
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The last step in any memory model is retrieval, or getting information out of memory so we can use it.
knowledge_points.plain: 从记忆中提取信息

knowledge_points.name: recognition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Recognition is the process of matching a current event or fact with one already in memory (e.g., “Have I smelled this smell before?”).
knowledge_points.plain: 把当前刺激与记忆匹配

knowledge_points.name: recall
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Recall is retrieving a memory with an external cue (e.g., “What does my Aunt Beki’s perfume smell like?”).
knowledge_points.plain: 依外部线索提取记忆

knowledge_points.name: retrieval cues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Both rely on retrieval cues, which are stimuli that help people retrieve memories.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助提取记忆的刺激

knowledge_points.name: tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This temporary inability to remember information is sometimes called the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon.
knowledge_points.plain: 暂时想不起来但觉得知道

knowledge_points.name: semantic network theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One theory that explains why this might work is the semantic network theory. This theory states that our brain might form new memories by connecting their meaning and context with meanings already in memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 记忆按语义相互连接成网

knowledge_points.name: flashbulb memories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Also called flashbulb memories, these memories are powerful because the importance of the event caused us to encode the context surrounding the event.
knowledge_points.plain: 对重大事件的生动记忆

knowledge_points.name: mood-congruent memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies consistently demonstrate the power of mood-congruent memory or the greater likelihood of recalling an item when our current mood matches the mood we were in when the event happened.
knowledge_points.plain: 情绪与记忆时相符更易提取

knowledge_points.name: state-dependent memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: State-dependent memory refers to the phenomenon of recalling events encoded while in particular states of consciousness.
knowledge_points.plain: 在相同意识状态下更易提取

knowledge_points.name: constructed memory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A constructed memory (or reconstructed memory) includes false details of a real event or might even be a recollection of an event that never occurred.
knowledge_points.plain: 含虚假细节或虚构事件的记忆

knowledge_points.name: misinformation effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies show that leading questions (questions or statements that purposefully include information or events that never happened—called the misinformation effect) can easily influence us to recall false details, and questioners can create an entirely new memory by repeatedly asking insistent questions.
knowledge_points.plain: 误导信息改变错误记忆细节

knowledge_points.name: decay
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One cause of forgetting is decay: forgetting because we do not use a memory or connections to a memory for a long period of time.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期不用导致记忆消退

knowledge_points.name: relearning effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you have to memorize the capitals again, it will take you less time than it did the first time you studied them.
knowledge_points.plain: 重学遗忘内容用时更少

knowledge_points.name: interference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another factor that causes forgetting is interference. Sometimes other information in your memory competes with what you are trying to recall.
knowledge_points.plain: 其他记忆干扰目标记忆提取

knowledge_points.name: retroactive interference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Learning new information interferes with the recall of older information.
knowledge_points.plain: 新学信息干扰旧信息提取

knowledge_points.name: proactive interference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Older information learned previously interferes with the recall of information learned more recently.
knowledge_points.plain: 旧信息干扰新信息提取

knowledge_points.name: intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Francis Galton was a pioneer in the study of human intelligence and testing.
knowledge_points.plain: 高尔顿开创的智力研究领域

knowledge_points.name: psychometricians
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although most teachers are experienced with creating tests, psychometricians are psychologists who specialize in making standardized tests.
knowledge_points.plain: 专门编制标准化测验的心理学家

knowledge_points.name: standardized test
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When we say that a test is standardized, we mean that the test items have been piloted on a similar population of people as those who are meant to take the test (the standardization sample) and that achievement norms have been established.
knowledge_points.plain: 经样本试测并建立常模的测验

knowledge_points.name: reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Reliability refers to the repeatability or consistency of the test as a means of measurement.
knowledge_points.plain: 测验结果的一致性或可重复性

knowledge_points.name: split-half reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Split-half reliability involves randomly dividing a test into two different sections and then correlating people’s performances on the two halves.
knowledge_points.plain: 两个半份测验分数相关

knowledge_points.name: equivalent-form reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The correlation between performance on the different forms of the test is known as equivalent-form reliability.
knowledge_points.plain: 不同等值版本分数相关

knowledge_points.name: test-retest reliability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, test-retest reliability refers to the correlation between a person’s score on one administration of the test with the same person’s score on a subsequent administration of the test.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一测验前后两次分数相关

knowledge_points.name: validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A test is valid when it measures what it is supposed to measure.
knowledge_points.plain: 测验测量到目标特质的程度

knowledge_points.name: face validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Face validity refers to a superficial measure of accuracy.
knowledge_points.plain: 表面上看是否测量了目标

knowledge_points.name: content validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Content validity refers to how well a measure reflects the entire range of material it is supposed to be testing.
knowledge_points.plain: 覆盖应测内容全范围的程度

knowledge_points.name: concurrent validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Concurrent validity measures how much of a characteristic a person has now.
knowledge_points.plain: 测量个体当前具有的特质

knowledge_points.name: predictive validity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Predictive validity is a measure of future performance.
knowledge_points.plain: 预测未来表现的能力

knowledge_points.name: aptitude tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Aptitude tests measure ability or potential
knowledge_points.plain: 测量能力或潜力的测验

knowledge_points.name: achievement tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: achievement tests measure what one has learned or accomplished
knowledge_points.plain: 测量已学知识或成就的测验

knowledge_points.name: speed tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Speed tests generally consist of a large number of questions asked in a short amount of time.
knowledge_points.plain: 限时完成大量题目的测验

knowledge_points.name: power tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The goal of a power test is to gauge the difficulty level of problems an individual can solve.
knowledge_points.plain: 测量能解决多难问题的测验

knowledge_points.name: group tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Group tests are administered to many people at a time.
knowledge_points.plain: 同时施测许多人的测验

knowledge_points.name: individual tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Individual tests involve greater interaction between the examiner and the examinee.
knowledge_points.plain: 需考官与受测者互动

knowledge_points.name: intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Typically, intelligence is defined as the ability to gather and use information in productive ways.
knowledge_points.plain: 收集并有效运用信息的能力

knowledge_points.name: g
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Intelligence can be measured by a single, general ability (g).
knowledge_points.plain: 斯皮尔曼提出的单一一般智力

knowledge_points.name: factor analysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: factor analysis, which is a statistical technique that measures the correlations between different items
knowledge_points.plain: 测量项目间相关性的统计方法

knowledge_points.name: multiple intelligences
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Theory of multiple intelligences—the term “intelligence” should be applied to a wide variety of abilities including kinesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic, verbal, spatial, and mathematical.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为智力包含多种能力

knowledge_points.name: intrapersonal intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Intrapersonal intelligence refers to one’s ability to understand oneself.
knowledge_points.plain: 理解自己内心世界的能力

knowledge_points.name: interpersonal intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Interpersonal intelligence, on the other hand, corresponds to a person’s ability to get along with and be sensitive to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 与他人相处并理解他人的能力

knowledge_points.name: naturalist intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, naturalist intelligence is found in people gifted at recognizing and organizing the things they encounter in the natural environment.
knowledge_points.plain: 识别并组织自然事物的能力

knowledge_points.name: triarchic theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Triarchic theory of intelligence—people can be intelligent in different ways; they can evidence analytic, practical, and creative intelligence.
knowledge_points.plain: 智力可分为分析实践创造三类

knowledge_points.name: Componential, or analytic, intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Componential, or analytic, intelligence involves the skills traditionally thought of as reflecting intelligence.
knowledge_points.plain: 传统智力测验所反映的能力

knowledge_points.name: creative intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The second type, experiential or creative intelligence, focuses on people’s ability to use their knowledge and experiences in new and innovative ways.
knowledge_points.plain: 用知识经验创新解决问题的能力

knowledge_points.name: practical intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with this type of intelligence are what we consider street-smart
knowledge_points.plain: 把知识用于现实情境的能力

knowledge_points.name: fluid intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Fluid intelligence refers to our ability to solve abstract problems and pick up new information and skills, while crystallized intelligence involves using knowledge accumulated over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 解决抽象问题并学习新技能

knowledge_points.name: crystallized intelligence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: crystallized intelligence involves using knowledge accumulated over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 运用长期积累的知识

knowledge_points.name: EQ
knowledge_points.definition_quote: EQ roughly corresponds to Gardner’s notions of interpersonal and intrapersonal intelligence.
knowledge_points.plain: 对应人际与内省智力的情商

knowledge_points.name: mental age
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Binet came up with the concept of mental age, an idea that presupposes that intelligence increases as one gets older.
knowledge_points.plain: 与生理年龄对应的智力年龄

knowledge_points.name: IQ
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A person’s IQ score on this test is computed by dividing the person’s mental age by his or her chronological age and multiplying by 100.
knowledge_points.plain: 心理年龄除以实际年龄乘一百

knowledge_points.name: deviation IQ
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Wechsler tests yield IQ scores based on what is known as deviation IQ. The tests are standardized so that the mean is 100, the standard deviation is 15, and the scores form a normal distribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 按标准差偏离均值计算智商

knowledge_points.name: Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS) is used in testing adults
knowledge_points.plain: 用于成人的韦氏智力测验

knowledge_points.name: Bias in testing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Interestingly, researchers seem to agree that although different races and genders may score differently on these tests, the tests have the same predictive validity for all groups.
knowledge_points.plain: 测验是否公平对待不同群体

knowledge_points.name: nature
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Keep in mind that nature refers to the influence of genetics, while nurture stresses the importance of the environment and learning.
knowledge_points.plain: 遗传对特质的影响

knowledge_points.name: nurture
knowledge_points.definition_quote: nurture stresses the importance of the environment and learning.
knowledge_points.plain: 环境与学习的影响

knowledge_points.name: heritability
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Heritability is a measure of how much of a trait’s variation is explained by genetic factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 遗传因素解释特质变异的比例

knowledge_points.name: Flynn effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Performance on intelligence tests has been increasing steadily throughout the century, a finding known as the Flynn effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 智力测验成绩随年代持续上升

knowledge_points.name: Monozygotic (identical) twins
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Monozygotic (identical) twins, who share 100 percent of their genetic material, score much more similarly on intelligence tests than do dizygotic (fraternal) twins, who have, on average, only 50 percent of their genes in common.
knowledge_points.plain: 同卵双胞胎智力分数更相似

knowledge_points.name: Head Start
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Participation in government programs such as Head Start, meant to redress some of the disadvantages faced by impoverished groups, has been shown to correlate with higher scores on intelligence tests.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助贫困儿童的政府早期项目

knowledge_points.name: differences within groups
knowledge_points.definition_quote: After putting the issue of cause aside, when comparing groups of people on any characteristic, keep in mind that differences within groups generally dwarf differences between groups.
knowledge_points.plain: 组内差异通常大于组间差异

knowledge_points.name: A CAUTIONARY NOTE
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Thus, we need to take care not to ascribe too great a meaning to a test score.
knowledge_points.plain: 不宜过度解读测验分数

knowledge_points.name: Developmental psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Developmental psychologists study how our behaviors and thoughts change over the course of our entire lives, from birth to death (or from conception to cremation).
knowledge_points.plain: 研究人一生中行为与思维的变化

knowledge_points.name: Nature versus nurture
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This chapter discusses influences on development from nature (genetic factors) first and then moves on to theories about nurture (environmental factors).
knowledge_points.plain: 先天遗传与后天环境的争论

knowledge_points.name: Cross-sectional research
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cross-sectional research uses participants of different ages to compare how certain variables may change over the lifespan.
knowledge_points.plain: 比较不同年龄组以研究变化

knowledge_points.name: Longitudinal research
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Instead of sampling from various age groups as in cross-sectional research, a longitudinal study examines one group of participants over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期追踪同一组受试者

knowledge_points.name: Genetics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our genes also help determine what abilities we are born with, such as our reflexes and our process of developing motor skills.
knowledge_points.plain: 基因影响先天能力发展

knowledge_points.name: Teratogens
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Certain chemicals or agents (called teratogens) can cause harm if ingested or contracted by the mother.
knowledge_points.plain: 可危害胎儿的化学物质或病原体

knowledge_points.name: Fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Children of alcoholic mothers who drink heavily during pregnancy are at high risk for fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS).
knowledge_points.plain: 孕期酗酒导致胎儿发育障碍

knowledge_points.name: Fetal alcohol effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researchers are also investigating a less severe effect of moderate drinking during pregnancy, fetal alcohol effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 孕期适度饮酒的较轻影响

knowledge_points.name: Reflexes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: All babies exhibit a set of reflexes, which are specific, inborn, automatic responses to certain specific stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 婴儿天生的自动反应

knowledge_points.name: Rooting reflex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When touched on the cheek, a baby will turn his or her head to the side where he or she felt the touch and seek to put the object into his or her mouth.
knowledge_points.plain: 触碰脸颊时婴儿转头寻食

knowledge_points.name: Sucking reflex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When an object is placed into the baby’s mouth, the infant will suck on it.
knowledge_points.plain: 吸吮入口中的物体

knowledge_points.name: Grasping reflex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If an object is placed into a baby’s palm or foot pad, the baby will try to grasp the object with his or her fingers or toes.
knowledge_points.plain: 抓握手掌或脚掌上的物体

knowledge_points.name: Moro reflex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When startled, a baby will fling his or her limbs out and then quickly retract them, making himself or herself as small as possible.
knowledge_points.plain: 受惊时四肢外展再收回

knowledge_points.name: Babinski reflex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When a baby’s foot is stroked, he or she will spread the toes.
knowledge_points.plain: 足底受刺激时脚趾张开

knowledge_points.name: Visual cliff
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some researchers develop innovative techniques like the visual cliff to measure what babies can perceive visually.
knowledge_points.plain: 测量婴儿深度知觉的实验装置

knowledge_points.name: Motor development
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Barring developmental difficulties, all humans develop the same basic motor skills in the same sequence, especially our gross motor skills like the examples described in this section.
knowledge_points.plain: 运动技能按固定顺序发展

knowledge_points.name: Gender roles
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Different cultures encourage different gender roles, which are behaviors that a culture associates with a gender.
knowledge_points.plain: 文化赋予性别的行为期望

knowledge_points.name: Biopsychological (Neuropsychological) Theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Biopsychological psychologists concentrate on the nature element in the nature/nurture combination that produces our gender roles.
knowledge_points.plain: 从生物因素解释性别角色

knowledge_points.name: Social-Cognitive Theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social-cognitive psychologists concentrate on the effects society and our own thoughts about gender have on role development.
knowledge_points.plain: 社会与认知影响性别角色发展

knowledge_points.name: Gender schema theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These psychologists focus on the internal interpretations we make about the gender messages we get from our environment (also known as gender schema theory).
knowledge_points.plain: 用内部解释理解性别信息

knowledge_points.name: Stage theories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Stage theories are, by definition, discontinuous theories of development.
knowledge_points.plain: 将发展视为分阶段突变的理论

knowledge_points.name: Zone of proximal development
knowledge_points.definition_quote: a child’s zone of proximal development is the range of tasks the child can perform independently and those tasks the child needs assistance with.
knowledge_points.plain: 儿童独立完成与需协助的任务范围

knowledge_points.name: Psychosocial stage theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He thought that our personality was profoundly influenced by our experiences with others, so he created the psychosocial stage theory. It consists of eight stages, each stage centering on a specific social conflict (see Table 11.2).
knowledge_points.plain: 人生八个阶段各含社会冲突

knowledge_points.name: Autonomy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Autonomy is our control over our own body, and Erikson thought that potty training was an early effort at gaining this control.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自身身体的控制

knowledge_points.name: Inferiority complex
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If we realize that we are behind or cannot do as well as our peers, which is having an inferiority complex, we may feel anxious about our performance in that area throughout the rest of the stages.
knowledge_points.plain: 因落后于同伴而产生的自卑

knowledge_points.name: Imaginary audience
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Other researchers connect this idea with the tendency of adolescents to think about how they are viewed by an imaginary audience and overestimate how much other people are thinking about or focusing on them.
knowledge_points.plain: 以为别人都在关注自己

knowledge_points.name: Schemata
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Piaget described how children viewed the world through schemata, cognitive rules we use to interpret the world.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释世界的认知规则

knowledge_points.name: Assimilation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Typically, we incorporate our experiences into these existing schemata in a process called assimilation.
knowledge_points.plain: 把新经验纳入已有认知规则

knowledge_points.name: Accommodation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sometimes, information does not fit into or violates our schemata, so we must accommodate and change our schemata.
knowledge_points.plain: 改变认知规则以适应新信息

knowledge_points.name: Object permanence
knowledge_points.subheading: Sensorimotor Stage (Birth to Approximately Two Years Old)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When babies start to look for or somehow acknowledge that objects do exist when they cannot see them, they have object permanence.
knowledge_points.plain: 物体看不见时仍然存在

knowledge_points.name: Egocentric
knowledge_points.subheading: Preoperational Stage (Two to Approximately Seven Years Old)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Children in this stage are also egocentric in their thinking since they cannot look at the world from anyone’s perspective but their own.
knowledge_points.plain: 只能从自己视角看世界

knowledge_points.name: Theory of mind
knowledge_points.subheading: Preoperational Stage (Two to Approximately Seven Years Old)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Modern developmental and cognitive psychologists call the ability to think about and consider the mental states of others the theory of mind.
knowledge_points.plain: 理解他人心理状态的能力

knowledge_points.name: Conservation
knowledge_points.subheading: Concrete Operational Stage (Eight to Approximately Twelve Years Old)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Piaget categorized children as being in the concrete operational stage when they demonstrated knowledge of concepts of conservation, the realization that properties of objects remain the same even when their shapes change.
knowledge_points.plain: 物体外形改变但属性不变

knowledge_points.name: Abstract reasoning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Through abstract reasoning, we can manipulate objects and contrast ideas in our mind without physically seeing them or having real-world correlates.
knowledge_points.plain: 脱离具体事物进行抽象思考

knowledge_points.name: Metacognition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Also, in the formal operational stage, we gain the ability to think about the way we think; this is called metacognition.
knowledge_points.plain: 思考自己的思维过程

knowledge_points.name: Personal fable
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This new ability to think abstractly can lead some adolescents into a different kind of egocentric thinking: they can develop a personal fable, which is a belief that they are unique or different from everyone else, or they can develop an attitude of superiority or invulnerability.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为自己独特且不会受伤害

knowledge_points.name: Information processing model
knowledge_points.subheading: Criticisms of Piaget: Information Processing Model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Information processing points out that our abilities to memorize, interpret, and perceive gradually develop as we age rather than developing in distinct stages.
knowledge_points.plain: 认知能力随年龄逐渐发展

knowledge_points.name: Phonemes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Phonemes are the smallest units of sound used in a language.
knowledge_points.plain: 语言中最小的语音单位

knowledge_points.name: Morpheme
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A morpheme is the smallest unit of meaningful sound.
knowledge_points.plain: 最小的有意义语音单位

knowledge_points.name: Syntax
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These words are then spoken or written in a particular order, called syntax.
knowledge_points.plain: 词语排列的规则

knowledge_points.name: Semantics
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The meanings of words, and the combinations of words in phrases and sentences, is referred to as semantics.
knowledge_points.plain: 词语及句子的意义

knowledge_points.name: Babbling stage
knowledge_points.definition_quote: First, if you have ever been around babies, you know that babies babble. This is often cute, and it is the first stage of language acquisition that occurs about four months of age.
knowledge_points.plain: 约四个月开始咿呀学语

knowledge_points.name: Holophrases
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The time during which babies speak in single words (holophrases) is sometimes called the holophrastic stage or one-word stage.
knowledge_points.plain: 用单个词表达意思的阶段

knowledge_points.name: Telegraphic speech
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The next language acquisition stage occurs at around 18 months and is called the telegraphic speech or two-word stage.
knowledge_points.plain: 约18个月开始说两个词

knowledge_points.name: Overgeneralization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This misapplication of grammar rules is called overgeneralization or overregularization.
knowledge_points.plain: 错误套用语法规则

knowledge_points.name: Language acquisition device
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researcher Noam Chomsky theorized that humans are born with a language acquisition device, the ability to learn a language rapidly as children.
knowledge_points.plain: 人类与生俱来的语言学习能力

knowledge_points.name: Critical period
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He theorized that a critical period (a window of opportunity during which we must learn a skill or our development will permanently suffer) for learning language may exist.
knowledge_points.plain: 必须学习某项技能的有限时期

knowledge_points.name: Linguistic relativity hypothesis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychologist Benjamin Whorf theorized that the language we use might control, and in some ways limit, our thinking. This theory is called the linguistic relativity hypothesis.
knowledge_points.plain: 语言影响并限制思维方式

knowledge_points.name: Attachment parenting
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some research focused on how attachment parenting, or the reciprocal relationship between caregiver and child, affects development.
knowledge_points.plain: 照护者与孩子间的互惠关系

knowledge_points.name: Imprinting
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Biologist Konrad Lorenz established that some infant animals (such as geese) become attached to (imprint on) individuals or even objects they see during a critical period after birth.
knowledge_points.plain: 幼动物出生后对所见对象依恋

knowledge_points.name: Contact comfort
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Harlow’s studies demonstrated the importance of physical comfort in the formation of attachment to parents.
knowledge_points.plain: 身体接触带来的舒适感有助依恋

knowledge_points.name: Temperament
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some researchers try to investigate the possible influences of attachment experiences on our later temperament— our emotional style or typical way we react to stressful situations.
knowledge_points.plain: 对压力的典型情绪反应风格

knowledge_points.name: Secure attachment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Infants with secure attachments (about 66 percent of the participants) confidently explored the novel environment while the parents were present, were distressed when the parents left, and came to the parents when they returned.
knowledge_points.plain: 安心探索、父母离开时不安

knowledge_points.name: Avoidant attachment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Infants with avoidant attachments (about 21 percent of the participants) resisted being held by the parents and explored the novel environment.
knowledge_points.plain: 回避与父母的身体接触

knowledge_points.name: Anxious/ambivalent attachment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Infants with anxious/ambivalent attachments (also called resistant attachments or insecure attachments, about 12 percent of the participants) had ambivalent reactions to the parents.
knowledge_points.plain: 对父母反应矛盾、既焦虑又抗拒

knowledge_points.name: Ecological systems theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This theory views human development as a system of relationships that is impacted by our environment.
knowledge_points.plain: 环境关系系统影响人的发展

knowledge_points.name: Microsystem
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Microsystem: direct interactions between the child and their immediate surroundings, including their caregivers.
knowledge_points.plain: 儿童与身边人的直接互动

knowledge_points.name: Mesosystem
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The mesosystem acknowledges that each of the five ecological systems interact.
knowledge_points.plain: 各微观系统之间的相互影响

knowledge_points.name: Exosystem
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Exosystem: this system involves indirect influences on the child’s development.
knowledge_points.plain: 对儿童发展的间接影响

knowledge_points.name: Macrosystem
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Macrosystem: influences of the cultures a child is immersed in will also influence his or her development.
knowledge_points.plain: 文化对儿童发展的影响

knowledge_points.name: Chronosystem
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Chronosystem: times of transition or change that occur over the chronology or timeline of a child’s life that influence development.
knowledge_points.plain: 人生时间线上的转变影响发展

knowledge_points.name: Authoritarian parents
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Authoritarian parents set strict standards for their children’s behavior and apply punishments for violations of these rules.
knowledge_points.plain: 严格立规并以惩罚执行

knowledge_points.name: Permissive parents
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Permissive parents do not set clear guidelines for their children.
knowledge_points.plain: 不设明确规则、管教宽松

knowledge_points.name: Authoritative parents
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Authoritative parents have set consistent standards for their children’s behavior, but the standards are reasonable and explained.
knowledge_points.plain: 规则合理且解释清楚

knowledge_points.name: Learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Learning is commonly defined as a long-lasting change in behavior resulting from experience.
knowledge_points.plain: 由经验引起的持久行为变化

knowledge_points.name: Classical conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As a result, Pavlov deduced the basic principle of classical conditioning (also called associative learning). People and animals can learn to associate neutral stimuli (e.g., sounds) with stimuli that produce reflexive, involuntary responses (e.g., food) and will learn to respond similarly to the new stimulus as they did to the old one (e.g., salivate).
knowledge_points.plain: 中性刺激与反应建立联结

knowledge_points.name: Unconditioned stimulus (US or UCS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The original stimulus that elicits a response is known as the unconditioned stimulus (US or UCS).
knowledge_points.plain: 天生引发反应的刺激

knowledge_points.name: Unconditioned response (UR or UCR)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Food elicits the natural, involuntary response of salivation. This response is called the unconditioned response (UR or UCR).
knowledge_points.plain: 对无条件刺激的自然反应

knowledge_points.name: Conditioned stimulus (CS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: the bell is no longer a neutral stimulus but, rather, a conditioned stimulus (CS)
knowledge_points.plain: 经条件作用能引发反应的刺激

knowledge_points.name: Conditioned response (CR)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: the bell elicits salivation, which is now a conditioned response (CR)
knowledge_points.plain: 经条件作用习得的反应

knowledge_points.name: Acquisition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This learning is also called acquisition since the animals have acquired a new behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 习得新行为的过程

knowledge_points.name: Delayed conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Generally, the most effective method of conditioning is to present the CS first and then to introduce the US while the CS is still evident.
knowledge_points.plain: 先呈现条件刺激再给无条件刺激

knowledge_points.name: Trace conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Trace conditioning—Presentation of the CS, followed by a short break, followed by presentation of the US.
knowledge_points.plain: 条件刺激后停顿再给无条件刺激

knowledge_points.name: Simultaneous conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Simultaneous conditioning—Presentation of the CS and US at the same time.
knowledge_points.plain: 条件与无条件刺激同时出现

knowledge_points.name: Backward conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Backward conditioning—Presentation of the US first, followed by presentation of the CS.
knowledge_points.plain: 先给无条件刺激再给条件刺激

knowledge_points.name: Extinction
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In psychological terminology, the process of unlearning a behavior is known as extinction.
knowledge_points.plain: 消除已习得的条件反应

knowledge_points.name: Spontaneous recovery
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sometimes, after a conditioned response has been extinguished and no further training of the animals has taken place, the response briefly reappears upon presentation of the conditioned stimulus.
knowledge_points.plain: 消退后反应短暂重现

knowledge_points.name: Generalization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This tendency to respond to similar CSs is known as generalization.
knowledge_points.plain: 对相似刺激产生相同反应

knowledge_points.name: Discrimination
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Subjects can be trained, however, to tell the difference, or discriminate, among various stimuli. This is called discrimination.
knowledge_points.plain: 区分相似刺激只对特定者反应

knowledge_points.name: Aversive conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This example is an illustration of what is known as aversion conditioning. Whereas Pavlov’s dogs were conditioned with something pleasant (food), baby Albert was conditioned to have a negative response to the white rat.
knowledge_points.plain: 将中性刺激与厌恶反应联结

knowledge_points.name: Higher-order conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Once a CS elicits a CR, it is possible, briefly, to use that CS as a US in order to condition a response to a new stimulus. This process is known as higher-order conditioning or second-order conditioning.
knowledge_points.plain: 用已条件化刺激再训练新刺激

knowledge_points.name: Taste aversion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you ingest an unusual food or drink and then become nauseous, you may develop an aversion to the food or drink.
knowledge_points.plain: 对某种味道食物的厌恶

knowledge_points.name: Biological preparedness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This type of powerful conditioning may occur because of biological preparedness: we are biologically predisposed to associate nausea with something we ate or drank.
knowledge_points.plain: 天生易形成某些联想

knowledge_points.name: Salient stimuli
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Salient stimuli are easily noticeable and therefore create a more powerful conditioned response.
knowledge_points.plain: 易于注意、条件反应更强

knowledge_points.name: Garcia effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The ease with which animals learn taste aversions is known as the Garcia effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 动物容易学会味觉厌恶

knowledge_points.name: Operant conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Whereas classical conditioning is a type of learning based on association of stimuli, operant conditioning is a kind of learning based on the association of consequences with one’s behaviors.
knowledge_points.plain: 行为后果与行为的联结

knowledge_points.name: Law of effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Thorndike put forth the law of effect that states that if the consequences of a behavior are pleasant, the stimulus-response (S- R) connection will be strengthened and the likelihood of the behavior will increase.
knowledge_points.plain: 愉快后果强化刺激反应联结

knowledge_points.name: Instrumental learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He used the term instrumental learning to describe his work because he believed the consequence was instrumental in shaping future behaviors.
knowledge_points.plain: 后果在塑造行为中起关键作用

knowledge_points.name: Reinforcer
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Reinforcement is defined by its consequences; anything that makes a behavior more likely to occur is a reinforcer.
knowledge_points.plain: 使行为更可能发生的刺激

knowledge_points.name: Positive reinforcement
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Positive reinforcement refers to the addition of something pleasant.
knowledge_points.plain: 增加愉快刺激以强化行为

knowledge_points.name: Negative reinforcement
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Negative reinforcement refers to the removal of something unpleasant.
knowledge_points.plain: 移除不快刺激以强化行为

knowledge_points.name: Escape learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Escape learning allows one to terminate an aversive stimulus; avoidance learning, on the other hand, enables one to avoid the unpleasant stimulus altogether.
knowledge_points.plain: 学会终止不愉快刺激

knowledge_points.name: Avoidance learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: avoidance learning, on the other hand, enables one to avoid the unpleasant stimulus altogether.
knowledge_points.plain: 学会预先避开不愉快刺激

knowledge_points.name: Punishment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: By definition, punishment is anything that makes a behavior less likely.
knowledge_points.plain: 使行为更不可能发生的后果

knowledge_points.name: Positive punishment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: positive punishment (usually referred to simply as punishment), which is the addition of something unpleasant
knowledge_points.plain: 增加不快刺激以减少行为

knowledge_points.name: Omission training
knowledge_points.definition_quote: omission training or negative punishment, which is the removal of something pleasant
knowledge_points.plain: 移除愉快刺激以减少行为

knowledge_points.name: Shaping
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Shaping reinforces the steps used to reach the desired behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 逐步强化接近目标的行为

knowledge_points.name: Chaining
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Animals can also be taught to perform several responses successively in order to get a reward. This process is known as chaining.
knowledge_points.plain: 把多个行为连成复杂活动

knowledge_points.name: Discriminative stimulus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Discrimination (also called reinforcement discrimination) would involve teaching the rat to press only a particular bar or to press the bar only under certain conditions (e.g., when a tone is sounded). In this last example, the tone is called a discriminative stimulus.
knowledge_points.plain: 特定情境下引发反应的信号

knowledge_points.name: Primary reinforcers
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Primary reinforcers are, in and of themselves, rewarding.
knowledge_points.plain: 本身即具有强化作用的刺激

knowledge_points.name: Secondary reinforcers
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Secondary reinforcers are things we have learned to value such as praise or the chance to play a video game.
knowledge_points.plain: 后天学会重视的强化物

knowledge_points.name: Generalized reinforcer
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Money is a special kind of secondary reinforcer, called a generalized reinforcer, because it can be traded for virtually anything.
knowledge_points.plain: 可交换多种强化物的强化物

knowledge_points.name: Token economy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In a token economy, every time people perform a desired behavior, they are given a token.
knowledge_points.plain: 用代币奖励目标行为

knowledge_points.name: Premack principle
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This idea, that the reinforcing properties of something depend on the situation, is expressed in the Premack principle. It explains that whichever of two activities is preferred can be used to reinforce the activity that is not preferred.
knowledge_points.plain: 用偏好的活动强化不偏好活动

knowledge_points.name: Continuous reinforcement
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When you are first teaching a new behavior, rewarding the behavior each time is best. This process is known as continuous reinforcement.
knowledge_points.plain: 每次目标行为都给予强化

knowledge_points.name: Partial-reinforcement effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In addition, according to the partial- reinforcement effect, behaviors will be more resistant to extinction if the animal has not been reinforced continuously.
knowledge_points.plain: 非连续强化使行为更难消退

knowledge_points.name: Fixed-ratio (FR) schedule
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A fixed-ratio (FR) schedule provides reinforcement after a set number of responses.
knowledge_points.plain: 固定次数反应后给予强化

knowledge_points.name: Variable-ratio (VR) schedule
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A variable-ratio (VR) schedule also provides reinforcement based on the number of bar presses, but that number varies.
knowledge_points.plain: 平均次数不定地给予强化

knowledge_points.name: Fixed-interval (FI) schedule
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A fixed-interval (FI) schedule requires that a certain amount of time elapses before a bar press will result in a reward.
knowledge_points.plain: 固定时间后首次反应获强化

knowledge_points.name: Variable-interval (VI) schedule
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A variable- interval (VI) schedule varies the amount of time required to elapse before a response will result in reinforcement.
knowledge_points.plain: 不定时间后首次反应获强化

knowledge_points.name: Instinctive drift
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The tendency for animals to forgo rewards to pursue their typical patterns of behavior is called instinctive drift.
knowledge_points.plain: 动物放弃奖励而按本能行事

knowledge_points.name: Contiguity model
knowledge_points.subheading: The Contingency Model of Classical Conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Pavlovian model of classical conditioning is known as the contiguity model because it postulates that the more times two things are paired, the greater the learning that will take place.
knowledge_points.plain: 配对次数越多学习越强

knowledge_points.name: Contingency model of classical conditioning
knowledge_points.subheading: The Contingency Model of Classical Conditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Rescorla’s contingency model of classical conditioning reflects more of a cognitive spin, positing that it is necessary for one event to reliably predict another for a strong association between the two to result.
knowledge_points.plain: 一事件可靠预测另一事件才形成联结

knowledge_points.name: Observational learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As you are no doubt aware, people and animals learn many things simply by observing others.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过观察他人进行学习

knowledge_points.name: Species specific
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This type of learning is said to be species specific; it occurs only among members of the same species.
knowledge_points.plain: 只发生在同一物种成员之间

knowledge_points.name: Modeling
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Modeling has two basic components: observation and imitation.
knowledge_points.plain: 观察并模仿他人行为

knowledge_points.name: Latent learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Latent means hidden, and latent learning is learning that becomes obvious only once a reinforcement is given for demonstrating it.
knowledge_points.plain: 奖励出现才显现的潜在学习

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive map
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He suggested they had made a mental representation, or cognitive map, of the maze during the first half of the trials and evidenced this knowledge once it would earn them a reward.
knowledge_points.plain: 对空间布局的心理表征

knowledge_points.name: Abstract learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Abstract learning involves understanding concepts such as tree or same rather than learning simply to press a bar or peck a disk to secure a reward.
knowledge_points.plain: 理解概念而非简单刺激反应

knowledge_points.name: Insight learning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Insight learning occurs when one suddenly realizes how to solve a problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 突然领悟问题解决办法

knowledge_points.name: Social psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social psychology is a broad field devoted to studying the way that people relate to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究人们如何与他人相处的学科

knowledge_points.name: Social cognition
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This field applies many of the concepts you learned about in the field of cognition, such as memory and biases, to help explain how people think about themselves and others.
knowledge_points.plain: 用认知规律解释人如何思考他人

knowledge_points.name: Social influence theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another key concept is social influence theory, the idea that how people feel and act is affected by the other people around them.
knowledge_points.plain: 周围人影响人的感受与行为

knowledge_points.name: Attribution theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Attribution theory tries to explain how people determine the cause of what they observe.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释人如何判断行为原因

knowledge_points.name: Dispositional attribution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For instance, if your friend Charley told you he got a perfect score on his math test, you might find yourself thinking that Charley is very good at math. In that case, you have made a dispositional attribution or person attribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 把行为归因于个人特质

knowledge_points.name: Situation attribution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Alternatively, you might attribute Charley’s success to a situational factor, such as an easy test; in that case, you make a situation attribution.
knowledge_points.plain: 把行为归因于情境因素

knowledge_points.name: Consistency
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Consistency refers to how similarly the individual acts in the same situation over time.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一情境中行为的一致程度

knowledge_points.name: Distinctiveness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Distinctiveness refers to how similar this situation is to other situations in which we have watched Charley.
knowledge_points.plain: 当前情境与其他情境的相似度

knowledge_points.name: Consensus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Consensus asks us to consider how others in the same situation have responded.
knowledge_points.plain: 看他人在同一情境中的反应

knowledge_points.name: Self-fulfilling prophecy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Even more interesting is the idea that the expectations we have of others can influence the way those others behave.
knowledge_points.plain: 期望促使他人按预期行事

knowledge_points.name: Fundamental attribution error
knowledge_points.definition_quote: When looking at the behavior of others, people tend to overestimate the importance of dispositional factors and underestimate the role of situational variables.
knowledge_points.plain: 解释他人时高估性格因素

knowledge_points.name: Actor-observer bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Whereas the fundamental attribution error focuses on how we explain others’ behavior, the actor-observer bias explains both the actor’s tendency to attribute behavior to situational factors and the observer’s tendency to attribute behavior to dispositional factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 自己归因情境他人归因性格

knowledge_points.name: False-consensus effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The tendency for people to overestimate the number of people who agree with them is called the false-consensus effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 高估他人与自己意见一致

knowledge_points.name: Self-serving bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-serving bias is the tendency to take more credit for good outcomes than for bad ones.
knowledge_points.plain: 好结果揽功坏结果推责

knowledge_points.name: Just-world phenomenon
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This belief in a just world, known simply as the just-world phenomenon or just-world bias, in which misfortunes befall people who deserve them, can be seen in the tendency to blame victims.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为人们遭遇都是应得的

knowledge_points.name: Attitude
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An attitude is a set of beliefs and feelings.
knowledge_points.plain: 对事物的信念与感受

knowledge_points.name: Mere exposure effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The mere exposure effect states that the more one is exposed to something, the more one will come to like it.
knowledge_points.plain: 接触越多越容易喜欢

knowledge_points.name: Elaboration likelihood model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: According to the elaboration likelihood model, persuasive messages can be processed through either the central route or the peripheral route.
knowledge_points.plain: 说服信息有两条加工路径

knowledge_points.name: Central route to persuasion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The central route to persuasion involves deeply processing the content of the message
knowledge_points.plain: 深入加工信息内容来说服

knowledge_points.name: Peripheral route
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The peripheral route, on the other hand, involves other aspects of the message, including the characteristics of the person imparting the message (the communicator).
knowledge_points.plain: 靠信息之外线索来说服

knowledge_points.name: LaPiere study
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In 1934, Richard LaPiere conducted an early study that illustrated this difference (see Table 13.2).
knowledge_points.plain: 态度不能完全预测行为

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive dissonance theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cognitive dissonance theory is based on the idea that people are motivated to have consistent attitudes and behaviors.
knowledge_points.plain: 态度行为不一致产生紧张

knowledge_points.name: Foot-in-the-door technique
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The foot- in-the-door technique suggests that if you can get people to agree to a small request, they will become more likely to agree to a follow-up request that is larger.
knowledge_points.plain: 先小请求后大请求

knowledge_points.name: Door-in-the-face technique
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The door-in-the-face technique argues that after people refuse a large request, they will look more favorably upon a follow- up request that seems, in comparison, much more reasonable.
knowledge_points.plain: 先大请求被拒再提小请求

knowledge_points.name: Norms of reciprocity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People tend to think that when someone does something nice for them, they ought to do something nice in return.
knowledge_points.plain: 受人恩惠应回报

knowledge_points.name: Social responsibility norm
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A related concept is the social responsibility norm, the belief that we all should do what we can to make the world and our society a better place.
knowledge_points.plain: 人人都应尽力改善社会

knowledge_points.name: Social trap
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A social trap is a situation in which the betterment of society requires us all to make some kind of sacrifice but our individual contribution is so small that people often choose to act in their own immediate interest instead of in the larger societal interest.
knowledge_points.plain: 个人私利导致集体受损

knowledge_points.name: Stereotypes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We all have ideas about what members of different groups are like, and these expectations may influence the way we interact with members of those groups. We call these ideas stereotypes.
knowledge_points.plain: 对某群体的概括看法

knowledge_points.name: Prejudice
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Prejudice is an undeserved, usually negative, attitude toward a group of people.
knowledge_points.plain: 对某群体不公正的负面态度

knowledge_points.name: Implicit attitude
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An explicit attitude is something someone is conscious of, while an implicit attitude is something that may influence someone’s behavior without their being aware of it.
knowledge_points.plain: 无意识影响行为的评价

knowledge_points.name: Ethnocentrism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Ethnocentrism, the belief that one’s culture (e.g., ethnic, racial) is superior to others, is a specific kind of prejudice.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为自己文化优于其他文化

knowledge_points.name: Discrimination
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Prejudice is an attitude, but discrimination involves an action.
knowledge_points.plain: 基于偏见采取的行动

knowledge_points.name: Out-group homogeneity bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People tend to see members of their own group, the in-group, as more diverse than members of other groups, the out-groups. This phenomenon is often referred to as out-group homogeneity bias.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为外群体成员都相似

knowledge_points.name: In-group bias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In addition, researchers have documented a preference for members of one’s own group, a kind of in-group bias.
knowledge_points.plain: 偏爱自己所属群体成员

knowledge_points.name: Categorization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some psychologists have suggested that people naturally and inevitably magnify differences between their own group and others as a function of the cognitive process of categorization.
knowledge_points.plain: 把人分类并夸大群体差异

knowledge_points.name: Contact theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The contact theory, as its name suggests, states that contact between hostile groups will reduce animosity but only if the groups are made to work toward a goal that benefits all and necessitates the participation of all.
knowledge_points.plain: 接触合作可减少敌意

knowledge_points.name: Superordinate goal
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The contact theory, as its name suggests, states that contact between hostile groups will reduce animosity but only if the groups are made to work toward a goal that benefits all and necessitates the participation of all. Such a goal is called a superordinate goal.
knowledge_points.plain: 需要群体共同合作的目标

knowledge_points.name: Instrumental aggression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Instrumental aggression is when the aggressive act is intended to secure a particular end.
knowledge_points.plain: 为达到某种目的的攻击

knowledge_points.name: Hostile aggression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Hostile aggression, on the other hand, has no such clear purpose.
knowledge_points.plain: 无明确目的的攻击

knowledge_points.name: Thanatos
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Freud linked aggression to Thanatos, the death instinct.
knowledge_points.plain: 弗洛伊德称攻击源于死本能

knowledge_points.name: Frustration-aggression hypothesis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One of the most influential theories, however, is known as the frustration-aggression hypothesis. This hypothesis holds that the feeling of frustration makes aggression more likely.
knowledge_points.plain: 挫折感增加攻击的可能性

knowledge_points.name: Bobo doll experiment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another common theory is that the exposure to aggressive models makes people aggressive as illustrated by Bandura, Ross, and Ross’s (1963) classic Bobo doll experiment.
knowledge_points.plain: 观察攻击榜样会学得攻击

knowledge_points.name: Prosocial behavior
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although social psychologists have devoted a lot of time and effort to studying antisocial behavior, they have also studied the factors that make people more likely to help one another. Such helping behavior is termed prosocial behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助他人的亲社会行为

knowledge_points.name: Bystander intervention
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Much of the research in this area has focused on bystander intervention, the conditions under which people nearby are more and are less likely to help someone in trouble.
knowledge_points.plain: 旁观者在什么条件下出手

knowledge_points.name: Bystander effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Counterintuitively, the larger the number of people who witness an emergency situation, the less likely any one is to intervene. This finding is known as the bystander effect.
knowledge_points.plain: 旁观者越多越少有人帮助

knowledge_points.name: Diffusion of responsibility
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One explanation for this phenomenon is called diffusion of responsibility. The larger the group of people who witness a problem, the less responsible any one individual feels to help.
knowledge_points.plain: 人越多个人责任感越弱

knowledge_points.name: Pluralistic ignorance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another factor contributing to the bystander effect is known as pluralistic ignorance. People seem to decide what constitutes appropriate behavior in a situation by looking to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 靠观察他人判断该如何做

knowledge_points.name: Similarity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although conventional wisdom holds that opposites attract, psychological research indicates that we are drawn to people who are similar to us, those who share our attitudes, backgrounds, and interests.
knowledge_points.plain: 人们喜欢与自己相似的人

knowledge_points.name: Proximity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Proximity means nearness.
knowledge_points.plain: 空间距离近容易产生吸引

knowledge_points.name: Reciprocal liking
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Thus, the more someone likes you, the more you will probably like that person.
knowledge_points.plain: 对方喜欢你你也更喜欢对方

knowledge_points.name: Self-disclosure
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One self-discloses when one shares a piece of personal information with another.
knowledge_points.plain: 分享个人私密信息

knowledge_points.name: Social facilitation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This phenomenon, that the presence of others improves task performance, is known as social facilitation.
knowledge_points.plain: 他人在场提高任务表现

knowledge_points.name: Social impairment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Later studies, however, found that when the task being observed was a difficult one rather than a simple, well-practiced skill, being watched by others actually hurt performance, a finding known as social impairment.
knowledge_points.plain: 他人在场降低困难任务表现

knowledge_points.name: Upward social comparison
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Upward social comparison is when we compare ourselves to people doing better than we are
knowledge_points.plain: 与比自己强的人比较

knowledge_points.name: Downward social comparison
knowledge_points.definition_quote: downward social comparison is when we compare ourselves to people doing worse than we are
knowledge_points.plain: 与比自己差的人比较

knowledge_points.name: Relative deprivation theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Relative deprivation theory explains that people tend to feel less satisfied with their lives when they engage in a lot of upward social comparison.
knowledge_points.plain: 向上比较降低生活满意度

knowledge_points.name: Conformity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Conformity is the tendency of people to go along with the views or actions of others.
knowledge_points.plain: 顺从群体观点或行为

knowledge_points.name: Normative social influence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Normative social influence is when people conform for social reasons—to belong to the group.
knowledge_points.plain: 为了归属群体而顺从

knowledge_points.name: Informational social influence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: On the other hand, informational social influence leads to conformity because people think the group knows best.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为群体更懂而顺从

knowledge_points.name: Obedience
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Although conformity involves following a group without being explicitly told to do so, obedience studies have focused on participants’ willingness to do what another asks them to do.
knowledge_points.plain: 按权威要求行事的意愿

knowledge_points.name: Norms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: All groups have norms, which are rules about how group members should act.
knowledge_points.plain: 群体成员应如何行事的规则

knowledge_points.name: Social loafing
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social loafing is the phenomenon when individuals do not put in as much effort when acting as part of a group as they do when acting alone.
knowledge_points.plain: 群体中个人努力减少

knowledge_points.name: Group polarization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Group polarization is the tendency of a group to make more extreme decisions than the group members would make individually.
knowledge_points.plain: 群体决策比个人更极端

knowledge_points.name: Groupthink
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Groupthink, a term coined by Irving Janis, describes the tendency for some groups to make bad decisions. Groupthink occurs when group members suppress their reservations about the ideas supported by the group.
knowledge_points.plain: 压制异议导致错误决策

knowledge_points.name: Deindividuation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This loss of self-restraint occurs when group members feel anonymous and aroused, and this phenomenon is known as deindividuation.
knowledge_points.plain: 匿名和兴奋下丧失自我约束

knowledge_points.name: Zimbardo’s prison experiment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One famous experiment that showed not only how such conditions can cause people to deindividuate but also the effect of roles and the situation in general is Philip Zimbardo’s prison experiment (see Table 13.2).
knowledge_points.plain: 角色扮演使人变得残忍

knowledge_points.name: Personality
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychologists define personality as the unique attitudes, behaviors, and emotions that characterize a person.
knowledge_points.plain: 个人独特的典型态度行为情感

knowledge_points.name: Type A
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Type A people tend to feel a sense of time pressure and are easily angered.
knowledge_points.plain: 有时间紧迫感易怒的人

knowledge_points.name: Type B
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Type B individuals, on the other hand, tend to be relaxed and easygoing.
knowledge_points.plain: 放松随和的人

knowledge_points.name: Id
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The id is in the unconscious and contains instincts and psychic energy.
knowledge_points.plain: 本能与心理能量的来源

knowledge_points.name: Ego
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The ego follows the reality principle, which means its job is to negotiate between the desires of the id and the limitations of the environment.
knowledge_points.plain: 协调本我与现实环境

knowledge_points.name: Superego
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Around the age of five, children begin to develop a conscience and to think about what is right and wrong. This sense of conscience, according to Freud, is their superego.
knowledge_points.plain: 内化的良心与是非感

knowledge_points.name: Defense mechanisms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The ego uses defense mechanisms to help protect the conscious mind.
knowledge_points.plain: 保护意识免受威胁的策略

knowledge_points.name: Repression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Blocking thoughts out from conscious awareness.
knowledge_points.plain: 把想法挡在意识之外

knowledge_points.name: Denial
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Not accepting the ego-threatening truth.
knowledge_points.plain: 拒绝接受威胁性事实

knowledge_points.name: Displacement
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Redirecting one’s feelings toward another person or object.
knowledge_points.plain: 把情绪转移到他人或物

knowledge_points.name: Projection
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Believing that the feelings one has toward someone else are actually held by the other person and directed at oneself.
knowledge_points.plain: 把自己的感受归为他人所有

knowledge_points.name: Reaction Formation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Expressing the opposite of how one truly feels.
knowledge_points.plain: 表现出与真实感受相反

knowledge_points.name: Regression
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Returning to an earlier, comforting form of behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 退回早期令人安心的行为

knowledge_points.name: Rationalization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Coming up with a beneficial result of an undesirable occurrence.
knowledge_points.plain: 为不好结果找出好处

knowledge_points.name: Intellectualization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Undertaking an academic, unemotional study of a topic.
knowledge_points.plain: 用学术方式冷静分析问题

knowledge_points.name: Sublimation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Channeling one’s frustration toward a different goal.
knowledge_points.plain: 把挫折转向其他目标

knowledge_points.name: Collective unconscious
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The collective unconscious is passed down through the species and, according to Jung, explains certain similarities we see among cultures.
knowledge_points.plain: 全人类共享的遗传潜意识

knowledge_points.name: Archetypes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The collective unconscious contains archetypes that Jung defined as universal concepts we all share as part of the human species.
knowledge_points.plain: 人类共有的普遍概念

knowledge_points.name: Inferiority
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Adler believed that people are motivated by the fear of failure, which he termed inferiority, and the desire to achieve, which he called superiority.
knowledge_points.plain: 害怕失败的自卑感

knowledge_points.name: Projective tests
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic theorists may use projective tests to try to delve into the unconscious. These tests involve asking people to interpret ambiguous stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 让受测者解释模糊刺激

knowledge_points.name: Rorschach inkblot test
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For instance, the Rorschach inkblot test involves showing people a series of inkblots and asking them to describe what they see.
knowledge_points.plain: 用墨迹图探测潜意识

knowledge_points.name: Thematic apperception test (TAT)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The thematic apperception test (TAT) consists of several cards, each of which contains a picture of a person or people in an ambiguous situation.
knowledge_points.plain: 用模糊图片编故事

knowledge_points.name: Determinism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Determinism is the belief that what happens is dictated by what has happened in the past.
knowledge_points.plain: 过去决定现在与未来

knowledge_points.name: Free will
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Neither theory supports the existence of free will, which is an individual’s ability to choose his or her own destiny.
knowledge_points.plain: 个人选择自己命运的能力

knowledge_points.name: Third force
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This perspective is often referred to as the third force because it arose in opposition to the determinism so central to both psychoanalytic and behaviorist models.
knowledge_points.plain: 人本主义被称为第三势力

knowledge_points.name: Self-concept
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-concept is a person’s global feeling about himself or herself.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自己整体的看法和感受

knowledge_points.name: Self-actualization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He believed that people are motivated to reach their full potential or self- actualize.
knowledge_points.plain: 发挥潜能实现自我

knowledge_points.name: Unconditional positive regard
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Unconditional positive regard is a kind of blanket acceptance.
knowledge_points.plain: 无条件的完全接纳

knowledge_points.name: Traits
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Trait theorists believe that we can describe people’s personalities by specifying their main characteristics, or traits.
knowledge_points.plain: 描述人格的稳定特征

knowledge_points.name: Nomothetic approach
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some trait theorists believe that the same basic set of traits can be used to describe all people’s personalities. Such a belief characterizes a nomothetic approach.
knowledge_points.plain: 用同一套特质描述所有人

knowledge_points.name: 16 PF
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Raymond Cattell developed the 16 PF (personality factor) test to measure what he believed were the 16 basic traits present in all people, albeit to different degrees.
knowledge_points.plain: 卡特尔16种人格因素测验

knowledge_points.name: Big Five personality traits
knowledge_points.definition_quote: More recently, Paul Costa and Robert McCrae have proposed that personality can be described using the Big Five personality traits: extroversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, openness to experience, and emotional stability (or neuroticism).
knowledge_points.plain: 用五个维度描述人格

knowledge_points.name: Factor analysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Factor analysis allows researchers to use correlations among traits to see which traits cluster together as factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 用相关找出特质群集

knowledge_points.name: Idiographic theorists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Other trait theorists, called idiographic theorists, assert that using the same set of terms to classify all people is impossible.
knowledge_points.plain: 主张逐一研究个体独特性

knowledge_points.name: Cardinal dispositions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: He suggested that a small number of people are so profoundly influenced by one trait that it plays a pivotal role in virtually everything they do. He referred to such traits as cardinal dispositions.
knowledge_points.plain: 主导个体一切行为的特质

knowledge_points.name: Central dispositions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As their names indicate, central dispositions have a larger influence on personality than secondary dispositions.
knowledge_points.plain: 影响较大的人格特质

knowledge_points.name: Reciprocal determinism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: His model is based on the idea of reciprocal determinism, also known as triadic reciprocality. These terms essentially mean that each of these three factors influences both of the other two in a constant, looplike fashion.
knowledge_points.plain: 人环境行为三者相互影响

knowledge_points.name: Self-efficacy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with high self-efficacy are optimistic about their own ability to get things done, whereas people with low self-efficacy feel a sense of powerlessness.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自己完成任务的信心

knowledge_points.name: Locus of control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A person can be described as having either an internal or an external locus of control.
knowledge_points.plain: 人对自己命运的控制感

knowledge_points.name: Internal locus of control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with an internal locus of control feel as if they are responsible for what happens to them.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为自己掌控命运

knowledge_points.name: External locus of control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Conversely, people with an external locus of control generally believe that luck and other forces outside of their own control determine their destinies.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为运气等外部力量决定命运

knowledge_points.name: Explanatory style
knowledge_points.definition_quote: We can also differentiate people by their explanatory style—the kind of attributions they make about the things that happen to them.
knowledge_points.plain: 对事件的归因习惯

knowledge_points.name: Optimistic explanatory style
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some people have an optimistic explanatory style, which leads them to make internal, global, and stable attributions for good things that happen to them and external, specific, and unstable attributions for bad experiences.
knowledge_points.plain: 好事归己坏事归外因

knowledge_points.name: Personality inventories
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Personality inventories are essentially questionnaires that ask people to provide information about themselves.
knowledge_points.plain: 让人自我报告的问卷

knowledge_points.name: MMPI-2
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI-2) is one of the most widely used self-report instruments.
knowledge_points.plain: 常用自评人格量表

knowledge_points.name: Barnum effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Research has demonstrated that people have the tendency to see themselves in vague, stock descriptions of personality.
knowledge_points.plain: 相信笼统描述适合自己

knowledge_points.name: Motivation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Motivations are feelings or ideas that cause us to act toward a goal.
knowledge_points.plain: 推动人朝目标行动的力量

knowledge_points.name: Instincts
