knowledge_points.definition_quote: If you have pets, you know that different animals are born with instincts, which are automatic behaviors performed in response to specific stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 天生对特定刺激的反应

knowledge_points.name: Drive reduction theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One early theory about how our physiology motivates us was drive reduction theory, the theory that our behavior is motivated by biological needs.
knowledge_points.plain: 行为由生理需要驱动

knowledge_points.name: Need
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A need is one of our requirements for survival, such as food, water, or shelter.
knowledge_points.plain: 生存所必需的条件

knowledge_points.name: Drive
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A drive is our impulse to act in a way that satisfies this need.
knowledge_points.plain: 满足需要的内在冲动

knowledge_points.name: Homeostasis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our body seeks homeostasis, which is a balanced internal state.
knowledge_points.plain: 身体追求的内部平衡状态

knowledge_points.name: Primary drives
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Primary drives are biological needs, like thirst.
knowledge_points.plain: 与生俱来的生理需要

knowledge_points.name: Secondary drives
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Secondary drives are learned drives.
knowledge_points.plain: 后天习得的驱力

knowledge_points.name: Arousal theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some motivations that seem to violate biological theories of motivation can be explained by arousal theory (or sensation- seeking theory), which states that we seek an optimum level of excitement or arousal.
knowledge_points.plain: 追求最佳唤醒水平

knowledge_points.name: Yerkes-Dodson law
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In general, most of us perform best with an optimal level of arousal, although this varies with different activities. We might perform well at an easy task with a very high level of arousal, but the same high level of arousal would prevent us from performing well on a difficult task.
knowledge_points.plain: 任务难度与最佳唤醒水平的关系

knowledge_points.name: Opponent-process theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, the theory states that we eventually feel an opponent process, meaning a motivation to return to our baseline, neutral state.
knowledge_points.plain: 偏离基线后产生反向动机

knowledge_points.name: Incentives
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Incentives are stimuli that we are drawn to due to learning.
knowledge_points.plain: 后天习得的有吸引力刺激

knowledge_points.name: Self-determination theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-determination research indicates that three elements are related to intrinsic motivations involved in what they call self- determination: autonomy, competence, and relatedness.
knowledge_points.plain: 内在动机基于三种需要

knowledge_points.name: Autonomy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Autonomy is the belief that we have the power to make choices that are important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 相信自己能自主选择

knowledge_points.name: Competence
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Competence is the belief that we have the skills and knowledge needed to accomplish tasks important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 相信自己具备完成任务的能力

knowledge_points.name: Relatedness
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Relatedness is our ability to form relationships with others who are important to us.
knowledge_points.plain: 与他人建立重要关系

knowledge_points.name: Hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The hypothalamus monitors and helps to control body chemistry (including the ratio of glucose and insulin) and makes us feel hungry when we need to eat.
knowledge_points.plain: 调节身体化学并产生饥饿感

knowledge_points.name: Lateral hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The lateral hypothalamus (hunger center), when stimulated, causes the animal to eat.
knowledge_points.plain: 刺激时促使进食的饥饿中枢

knowledge_points.name: Ventromedial hypothalamus
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another part of the hypothalamus, the ventromedial hypothalamus (satiety center), causes the animal to stop eating when it is stimulated.
knowledge_points.plain: 刺激时停止进食的饱食中枢

knowledge_points.name: Ghrelin
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Ghrelin influences short-term hunger; it’s produced in the stomach and communicates hunger to the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 胃分泌的短期饥饿激素

knowledge_points.name: Leptin
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Leptin is produced by fat cells and signals the brain that you have sufficient stored energy and thus are not hungry.
knowledge_points.plain: 脂肪细胞分泌的饱腹信号

knowledge_points.name: Set-point theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Set-point theory describes how the hypothalamus might decide what impulse to send. This theory states that the hypothalamus wants to maintain a certain optimum body weight.
knowledge_points.plain: 下丘脑维持理想体重设定点

knowledge_points.name: Externals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For example, research indicates that some of us (called externals) are more motivated to eat by external food cues, such as attractiveness or availability of food.
knowledge_points.plain: 易受外部食物线索影响者

knowledge_points.name: Internals
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Others (called internals) are less affected by the presence and presentation of food and respond more often to internal hunger cues.
knowledge_points.plain: 更依内部饥饿信号进食者

knowledge_points.name: Garcia effect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This is caused by the Garcia effect and occurs whenever nausea is paired with either food or drink.
knowledge_points.plain: 恶心与食物配对形成厌恶

knowledge_points.name: Bulimia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with bulimia eat large amounts of food in a short period of time (binging) and then get rid of the food (purging) by vomiting, exercising excessively, or using laxatives.
knowledge_points.plain: 暴食后催吐或清除食物

knowledge_points.name: Anorexia nervosa
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with anorexia starve themselves to below 85 percent of their normal body weight and refuse to eat due to their obsession with weight.
knowledge_points.plain: 因执着体重而极度节食

knowledge_points.name: Sexual response cycle
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The famous lab studies done by William Masters and Virginia Johnson documented the sexual response cycle in men and women.
knowledge_points.plain: 性反应经历四个阶段

knowledge_points.name: Refractory period
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Male systems experience a refractory period—a time period that must elapse before another orgasm.
knowledge_points.plain: 男性再次高潮前的恢复期

knowledge_points.name: Sexual desire
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sexual desire can be present even when the capability to have sex is lost.
knowledge_points.plain: 性能力丧失后仍有性欲

knowledge_points.name: Kinsey Reports
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Researchers (like Alfred Kinsey, who documented the variety of human sexual behaviors in the famous Kinsey Reports from the 1940s and 1950s) have been able to dispel some common myths about sexuality.
knowledge_points.plain: 金赛报告记录性行为多样性

knowledge_points.name: Sexual orientation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies show that gay and lesbian sexual orientation is not related to traumatic childhood experiences, parenting styles, the quality of relationships with parents, masculinity or femininity, or the sexual orientation of our parents.
knowledge_points.plain: 性取向与养育方式无关

knowledge_points.name: Achievement motivation
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Achievement motivation examines our desires to master complex tasks and knowledge and to reach personal goals.
knowledge_points.plain: 掌握任务与达成目标的动机

knowledge_points.name: Extrinsic motivations
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Extrinsic motivations are rewards that we get for accomplishments from outside ourselves (for example, grades, salary, and so on).
knowledge_points.plain: 来自外部的奖励

knowledge_points.name: Intrinsic motivations
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Intrinsic motivations are rewards we get internally, such as enjoyment or satisfaction.
knowledge_points.plain: 来自内部的满足感

knowledge_points.name: Theory X
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Theory X Managers believe that employees will work only if rewarded with benefits or threatened with punishment.
knowledge_points.plain: 管理者认为员工只为奖惩工作

knowledge_points.name: Theory Y
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Theory Y Managers believe that employees are internally motivated to do good work and policies should encourage this internal motive.
knowledge_points.plain: 管理者相信员工内在动机

knowledge_points.name: Approach-approach conflict
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The first, named an approach-approach conflict, occurs when you must choose between two desirable outcomes.
knowledge_points.plain: 在两个都想得到的目标间选择

knowledge_points.name: Avoidance-avoidance conflict
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another type of conflict, an avoidance-avoidance conflict, occurs when you must choose between two unattractive outcomes.
knowledge_points.plain: 在两个都不想要的目标间选择

knowledge_points.name: Approach-avoidance conflict
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An approach-avoidance conflict exists when one event or goal has both attractive and unattractive features.
knowledge_points.plain: 同一目标既有吸引力又令人排斥

knowledge_points.name: Multiple approach-avoidance conflicts
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, people experience multiple approach-avoidance conflicts. In these, you must choose between two or more things, each of which has both desirable and undesirable features.
knowledge_points.plain: 多个各有利弊的选项间选择

knowledge_points.name: James-Lange theory
knowledge_points.subheading: What Comes First—The Emotion or the Physiological Change?
knowledge_points.definition_quote: They theorized that we feel emotion because of biological changes caused by stress.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理变化在先情绪在后

knowledge_points.name: Facial feedback hypothesis
knowledge_points.subheading: What Comes First—The Emotion or the Physiological Change?
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The facial feedback hypothesis is a related idea that suggests that we infer our emotions from our facial expressions.
knowledge_points.plain: 根据面部表情推断情绪

knowledge_points.name: Cannon-Bard theory
knowledge_points.subheading: What Comes First—The Emotion or the Physiological Change?
knowledge_points.definition_quote: They theorized that the biological change and the cognitive awareness of the emotional state occur simultaneously.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理变化与情绪认知同时发生

knowledge_points.name: Two-factor theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Schachter pointed out that both our physical responses and our cognitive appraisal of them (our mental interpretations) combine to cause any particular emotional response.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理唤醒加认知标签形成情绪

knowledge_points.name: Broaden-and-build theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another theory of emotion known as the broaden-and-build theory focuses specifically on the power and potential of positive emotions. This theory contends that positive emotions facilitate a playful and experimental mindset, which makes it easier for people to expand their social interactions and try new activities.
knowledge_points.plain: 积极情绪拓展思维与行动

knowledge_points.name: Facial expressions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: No matter what culture we grew up in, we are likely to use the same facial expressions for basic emotions like happiness, sadness, anger, disgust, surprise, and fear.
knowledge_points.plain: 基本情绪的面部表情跨文化一致

knowledge_points.name: Sociobiology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This area of research (sometimes called sociobiology) indicates that the facial expressions we make for basic emotions may be an innate part of our physiological makeup.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究表情的先天生理基础

knowledge_points.name: Display rules
knowledge_points.definition_quote: On the other hand, researchers have documented some differences in how people express emotion. One cause is thought to be different cultural display rules.
knowledge_points.plain: 文化规定情绪表达方式

knowledge_points.name: Health
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Health is an important area of interest for psychologists.
knowledge_points.plain: 身心健康是心理学重要领域

knowledge_points.name: Psychological factors
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychological factors can affect physical factors as well as mental ones, and psychologists study how to encourage people to live healthy lives, manage stress, grow emotionally, and deal with mental illness.
knowledge_points.plain: 心理因素会影响身体健康

knowledge_points.name: Stress
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The term stress can refer to either certain life events (stressors) or how we react to these changes in the environment (stress reactions).
knowledge_points.plain: 压力指生活事件或应激反应

knowledge_points.name: social readjustment rating scale (SRRS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Their social readjustment rating scale (SRRS) measured stress using life change units (LCUs).
knowledge_points.plain: 用生活变化单位测量压力

knowledge_points.name: life change units (LCUs)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Different changes in life were assigned different LCUs; making a career change would be counted as more LCUs than moving to a new apartment.
knowledge_points.plain: 不同生活变化对应不同分数

knowledge_points.name: general adaptation syndrome (GAS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Hans Selye’s general adaptation syndrome (GAS) describes the general response humans and other animals have to a stressful event.
knowledge_points.plain: 面对压力的一般生理反应模式

knowledge_points.name: Alarm reaction
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our heart rate increases, and blood is diverted away from other body functions to muscles that are needed to react.
knowledge_points.plain: 心跳加快、血液流向肌肉

knowledge_points.name: Resistance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Our body remains physiologically ready (high heart rate, and so on). Hormones are released to maintain this state of readiness.
knowledge_points.plain: 身体保持生理戒备状态

knowledge_points.name: Exhaustion
knowledge_points.definition_quote: If the resistance stage lasts too long, our body can deplete its resources.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期抵抗耗尽身体资源

knowledge_points.name: tend-and-befriend theory
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some people successfully manage stress by actively seeking ways to tend to their own self-care needs and attend to the needs of friends and family members.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过照顾他人来减压

knowledge_points.name: emotion-focused coping
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some people use specific stress management techniques such as meditation/mindfulness exercises, breathing techniques, or combining these stress management techniques with medications prescribed by clinical psychologists.
knowledge_points.plain: 用冥想呼吸等方式调节情绪

knowledge_points.name: perceived control
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Control over events tends to lessen stress, while a perceived lack of control generally makes the event more stressful.
knowledge_points.plain: 对事件的控制感影响压力

knowledge_points.name: Positive psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The field of positive psychology emerged in the 1990s to counter what some saw as the overly negative focus of psychology on human error, weakness, and sickness.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究人类优势与幸福的心理学

knowledge_points.name: subjective well-being
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One area studied by positive psychologists is subjective well-being, which is a sense of how satisfied a person is with their life overall.
knowledge_points.plain: 对整体生活满意度的感受

knowledge_points.name: character strengths
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Positive psychology researchers investigate how aspects of personality they call character strengths or virtues can be measured and how using these strengths relates to life satisfaction and achievement.
knowledge_points.plain: 可测量的积极人格特质

knowledge_points.name: six core virtues
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These researchers identify six core virtues that seem to be valued across all major religions and philosophies: wisdom, courage, humanity, justice, temperance, and transcendence.
knowledge_points.plain: 跨文化重视的六种美德

knowledge_points.name: well-being
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Well-being refers to our perception of how effectively we function in our personal lives and our role in the groups to which we belong.
knowledge_points.plain: 对生活质量的整体感知

knowledge_points.name: gratitude
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Practicing gratitude (by expressing thankfulness toward others verbally or in writing) is associated with increases in our perceptions of happiness and satisfaction in life
knowledge_points.plain: 表达感谢能提升幸福感

knowledge_points.name: resilience
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Studies indicate that some people are more able to adapt effectively when faced with trauma and extreme stress and that some people experience post-traumatic growth after these intensely negative experiences.
knowledge_points.plain: 面对创伤仍能良好适应

knowledge_points.name: post-traumatic growth
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One concept positive psychologists talk about with regard to stress and difficult situations is post-traumatic growth, which is the ability to construct a meaningful experience in response to a period of trauma.
knowledge_points.plain: 创伤后获得积极成长

knowledge_points.name: Psychological disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychological disorders may manifest in a person’s behavior and/or thoughts.
knowledge_points.plain: 心理障碍可表现在行为或思维

knowledge_points.name: abnormal psychology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The field of psychological disorders (or abnormal psychology) encompasses the study of relatively common problems such as depression, substance abuse, and learning difficulties as well as the study of fairly rare, and particularly severe, disorders such as bipolar disorder and schizophrenia.
knowledge_points.plain: 研究心理障碍的心理学分支

knowledge_points.name: Psychological disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Disorders are often characterized by causing dysfunction, by resulting in distress, and as being deviant (different) from what is typical.
knowledge_points.plain: 以功能失调、痛苦、异常为特征

knowledge_points.name: insanity
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The reason behind the legal definition of insanity is to differentiate between those people who can be held entirely responsible for their crimes (the sane) and those people who, because of a psychological disorder, cannot be held fully responsible for their actions.
knowledge_points.plain: 判定刑事责任的法律概念

knowledge_points.name: International Classification of Mental Disorders (ICD)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The World Health Organization (WHO) created the International Classification of Mental Disorders (ICD) for this purpose, and the American Psychiatric Association uses the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM).
knowledge_points.plain: 世卫组织的疾病分类手册

knowledge_points.name: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The DSM, as its name suggests, provides a way for psychologists to diagnose their patients.
knowledge_points.plain: 美国精神障碍诊断手册

knowledge_points.name: etiologies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: These resources do not include much discussion of the causes (also called etiologies) or treatments of the various disorders, because adherents to each of the psychological perspectives disagree (see Table 17.1).
knowledge_points.plain: 心理障碍的成因

knowledge_points.name: biomedical model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: the biomedical model (or biological perspective) sees psychological disorders as caused by biological factors such as hormonal or neurotransmitter imbalances or by differences in brain structure.
knowledge_points.plain: 从生物因素解释心理障碍

knowledge_points.name: biopsychosocial view
knowledge_points.definition_quote: the biopsychosocial view is that problems likely result from the interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors.
knowledge_points.plain: 生物心理社会因素共同作用

knowledge_points.name: diathesis-stress model
knowledge_points.definition_quote: According to this model, environmental stressors can provide circumstances under which a biological predisposition for illness can express itself.
knowledge_points.plain: 压力触发先天的易感素质

knowledge_points.name: eclectic
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychologists who do not subscribe strictly to one perspective or another are known as eclectic.
knowledge_points.plain: 兼用多种理论观点

knowledge_points.name: autism spectrum disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Children with autism spectrum disorder seek out less social and emotional contact than do other children and are less likely to seek out parental support when distressed.
knowledge_points.plain: 社交与情感互动较少

knowledge_points.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A child with ADHD may have difficulty paying attention or sitting still.
knowledge_points.plain: 注意力难集中、坐不住

knowledge_points.name: neurocognitive disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The DSM-5 also discusses neurocognitive disorders, the most well-known of which may be Alzheimer’s disease.
knowledge_points.plain: 认知能力退化的障碍

knowledge_points.name: Alzheimer’s disease
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Alzheimer’s is a form of dementia, a deterioration of cognitive abilities, often seen most dramatically in memory.
knowledge_points.plain: 以记忆衰退为主的痴呆症

knowledge_points.name: Anxiety disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Anxiety disorders, as their name suggests, share a common symptom of anxiety.
knowledge_points.plain: 以焦虑为共同症状

knowledge_points.name: specific phobia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A simple or specific phobia is an intense unwarranted fear of a situation or an object such as claustrophobia (fear of enclosed spaces) or arachnophobia (fear of spiders).
knowledge_points.plain: 对特定事物不合理的恐惧

knowledge_points.name: agoraphobia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Agoraphobia is a fear of open, public spaces.
knowledge_points.plain: 害怕开阔或公共空间

knowledge_points.name: social anxiety disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Social anxiety disorder, formerly known as social phobia, is a fear of a situation in which one could embarrass oneself in public, such as when eating in a restaurant or giving a lecture.
knowledge_points.plain: 害怕在公众场合出丑

knowledge_points.name: taijin kyofusho
knowledge_points.definition_quote: It is a type of social anxiety that involves concern that one’s body is displeasing to others.
knowledge_points.plain: 日本文化中的社交焦虑

knowledge_points.name: generalized anxiety disorder (GAD)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A person who suffers from generalized anxiety disorder, often referred to as GAD, experiences constant, low-level anxiety.
knowledge_points.plain: 持续低水平的焦虑

knowledge_points.name: panic disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: On the other hand, someone with panic disorder suffers from acute episodes of intense anxiety without any apparent provocation.
knowledge_points.plain: 无明显诱因的急性焦虑

knowledge_points.name: Psychodynamic theorists on anxiety disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Anxiety Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic theorists see psychological disorders as caused by unresolved, unconscious conflicts.
knowledge_points.plain: 无意识冲突导致焦虑

knowledge_points.name: Behaviorists on anxiety disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Anxiety Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Behaviorists believe all behaviors are learned. Therefore, they assert that anxiety disorders are learned.
knowledge_points.plain: 焦虑是习得的反应

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive theorists
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Anxiety Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cognitive theorists believe that disorders result from dysfunctional ways of thinking.
knowledge_points.plain: 适应不良的思维方式致病

knowledge_points.name: Somatic symptom disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Somatic symptom disorders occur when a person manifests a psychological problem through a physiological symptom.
knowledge_points.plain: 心理问题表现为躯体症状

knowledge_points.name: conversion disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People who have conversion disorder report the existence of a severe physical problem such as paralysis or blindness, and they will, in fact, be unable to move their arms or see.
knowledge_points.plain: 无生理原因的躯体功能丧失

knowledge_points.name: Psychodynamic theorists on somatic symptom disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Somatic Symptom Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic theorists would assert that somatic symptom disorders are merely outward manifestations of unresolved unconscious conflicts.
knowledge_points.plain: 无意识冲突的向外表现

knowledge_points.name: Behaviorists on somatic symptom disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Somatic Symptom Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Behaviorists would say that people with somatic symptom disorders are being reinforced for their behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 躯体症状受到强化

knowledge_points.name: Dissociative disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Dissociative disorders involve a disruption in conscious processes; dissociation involves a break or separation from memories and thoughts or even a sense of who the person is.
knowledge_points.plain: 意识、记忆或身份出现断裂

knowledge_points.name: Dissociative amnesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Dissociative amnesia is when a person cannot remember things and no physiological basis for the disruption in memory can be identified.
knowledge_points.plain: 无生理原因的记忆丧失

knowledge_points.name: organic amnesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Biologically induced amnesia is called organic amnesia.
knowledge_points.plain: 生理原因导致的失忆

knowledge_points.name: Dissociative identity disorder (DID)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Dissociative identity disorder, formerly known as multiple personality disorder, is when a person has several personalities rather than one integrated personality.
knowledge_points.plain: 一个人表现出多重人格

knowledge_points.name: Psychodynamic theorists on dissociative disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Dissociative Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic theorists believe that dissociative disorders result when an extremely traumatic event has been so thoroughly repressed that a split in consciousness results.
knowledge_points.plain: 创伤被压抑导致意识分裂

knowledge_points.name: Behaviorists on dissociative disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Dissociative Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Behaviorists posit that people who have experienced trauma simply find not thinking about it to be rewarding, thus producing amnesia or, in extreme cases, DID.
knowledge_points.plain: 不去想创伤得到强化

knowledge_points.name: mood or affective disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Someone with a mood or affective disorder experiences extreme or inappropriate emotions.
knowledge_points.plain: 情绪极端或不恰当

knowledge_points.name: Major depressive disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Major depressive disorder, also known as unipolar depression, is the most common mood disorder and is often referred to as the common cold of all psychological disorders.
knowledge_points.plain: 最常见的心境障碍

knowledge_points.name: Persistent depressive disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Persistent depressive disorder is diagnosed when the depression is long-lasting but not as severe.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期但较轻的抑郁

knowledge_points.name: Seasonal affective disorder (SAD)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Finally, some people experience depression but only during certain times of the year, usually winter when there is less sunlight.
knowledge_points.plain: 季节变化引发的抑郁

knowledge_points.name: Psychodynamic theorists on depressive disorders
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Depressive Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic theorists may view depression as the product of anger directed inward or an overly punitive superego.
knowledge_points.plain: 愤怒内投或超我过严

knowledge_points.name: Learning theorists
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Depressive Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Learning theorists view the mood disorder as bringing about some kind of reinforcement such as attention or sympathy.
knowledge_points.plain: 抑郁带来关注与同情

knowledge_points.name: cognitive triad
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Depressive Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Aaron Beck, a cognitive theorist, believed that depression results from unreasonably negative ideas that people have about themselves, their world, and their futures. Beck calls these three components the cognitive triad.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自我世界未来的消极看法

knowledge_points.name: attribution
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Depressive Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An attribution is an explanation of cause.
knowledge_points.plain: 对原因的解释

knowledge_points.name: internal, global, and stable attributions
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Depressive Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People who tend to make internal, global, and stable attributions for bad events are more likely to be depressed.
knowledge_points.plain: 把坏事归于内在普遍稳定因素

knowledge_points.name: learned helplessness
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Depressive Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Learned helplessness is when one’s prior experiences have caused that person to view himself or herself as unable to control aspects of the future that are controllable.
knowledge_points.plain: 认为无法控制未来而放弃

knowledge_points.name: bipolar disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Unlike unipolar depression, bipolar disorder, formerly known as manic depression, usually involves both depressed and manic episodes.
knowledge_points.plain: 抑郁与躁狂交替出现

knowledge_points.name: manic episodes
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People experience manic episodes in different ways, but they usually involve feelings of high energy.
knowledge_points.plain: 精力异常旺盛的发作期

knowledge_points.name: hypomania
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The major difference is that bipolar II involves at least one episode of hypomania, which is a less extreme level of mania than in bipolar I.
knowledge_points.plain: 程度较轻的躁狂

knowledge_points.name: schizophrenia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The fundamental symptom of schizophrenia is disordered, distorted thinking often demonstrated through delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking, disorganized speech, and/or disorganized motor behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 思维紊乱、脱离现实的精神病

knowledge_points.name: delusions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Delusions are beliefs that have no basis in reality.
knowledge_points.plain: 与现实不符的错误信念

knowledge_points.name: hallucinations
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Hallucinations are perceptions in the absence of any sensory stimulation.
knowledge_points.plain: 无外界刺激的知觉

knowledge_points.name: neologisms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: They may make up their own words (neologisms) or string together a series of nonsense words that rhyme (clang associations).
knowledge_points.plain: 自创无意义的新词

knowledge_points.name: word salad
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As a result, it may be difficult to understand what they are trying to communicate, and the resultant speech has been described as word salad.
knowledge_points.plain: 杂乱无章、难以理解的言语

knowledge_points.name: flat affect
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Alternatively, they may consistently have essentially no emotional response at all (flat affect).
knowledge_points.plain: 几乎没有情绪反应

knowledge_points.name: catatonia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Some schizophrenics suffer from catatonia, a motor problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 运动行为异常

knowledge_points.name: positive symptoms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Positive symptoms refer to excesses in behavior, thought, or mood such as neologisms and hallucinations
knowledge_points.plain: 行为思维或情绪的过度

knowledge_points.name: negative symptoms
knowledge_points.definition_quote: negative symptoms correspond to deficits such as flat affect or catatonic stupor
knowledge_points.plain: 正常功能的缺失

knowledge_points.name: dopamine hypothesis
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Schizophrenic Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The basic idea behind the dopamine hypothesis is that high levels of dopamine seem to be associated with schizophrenia.
knowledge_points.plain: 多巴胺水平过高致病

knowledge_points.name: tardive dyskinesia
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Schizophrenic Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, extensive use of these drugs may also cause negative side effects such as muscle tremors and stiffness, a problem known as tardive dyskinesia.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期用药致肌肉震颤

knowledge_points.name: double bind
knowledge_points.subheading: Theories About the Cause of Schizophrenic Disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: A double bind is when a person is given contradictory messages.
knowledge_points.plain: 收到互相矛盾的信息

knowledge_points.name: Personality disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Personality disorders are well-established, maladaptive ways of behaving that negatively affect people’s ability to function.
knowledge_points.plain: 长期适应不良的行为模式

knowledge_points.name: Cluster A
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cluster A is associated with suspicious or eccentric behaviors and includes paranoid, schizoid, and schizotypal personality disorders.
knowledge_points.plain: 多疑古怪的行为集群

knowledge_points.name: Cluster B
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Cluster B is marked by impulsive or emotional, dramatic, and erratic tendencies and includes antisocial, histrionic, narcissistic, and borderline personality disorders.
knowledge_points.plain: 冲动戏剧化的行为集群

knowledge_points.name: antisocial personality disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: People with antisocial personality disorder have little regard for other people’s feelings.
knowledge_points.plain: 漠视他人感受与权利

knowledge_points.name: borderline personality disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Borderline personality disorder can result in unstable social relationships; people who suffer from it can fear abandonment and switch back and forth between how they feel about and act toward others.
knowledge_points.plain: 人际关系与情绪不稳定

knowledge_points.name: narcissistic personality disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Narcissistic personality disorder involves seeing oneself as the center of the universe (narcissism means “self-love”), and histrionic personality disorder connotes overly dramatic behavior (histrionics).
knowledge_points.plain: 以自我为中心

knowledge_points.name: Cluster C
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Anxiety is the hallmark of Cluster C, which includes avoidant, dependent, and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders.
knowledge_points.plain: 以焦虑为特征的行为集群

knowledge_points.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is when persistent, unwanted thoughts (obsessions) cause someone to feel the need (compulsion) to engage in a particular action.
knowledge_points.plain: 强迫思维引发强迫行为

knowledge_points.name: body dysmorphic disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, the DSM-5 has created a separate classification for OCD and related disorders, including hoarding disorder and body dysmorphic disorder (an obsession with perceived defects related to one’s appearance).
knowledge_points.plain: 过度担心外貌缺陷

knowledge_points.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: PTSD usually involves flashbacks or nightmares following a person’s involvement in or observation of an extremely troubling event such as a war or natural disaster.
knowledge_points.plain: 创伤后反复闪回或噩梦

knowledge_points.name: Paraphilias
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Paraphilias, or psychosexual disorders, are marked by the sexual attraction to an object, a person, or an activity not usually seen as sexual.
knowledge_points.plain: 非常规对象引发的性唤起

knowledge_points.name: pedophilia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: For instance, attraction to children is called pedophilia, to animals is called zoophilia, and to objects, such as shoes, is called fetishism.
knowledge_points.plain: 对儿童的性吸引

knowledge_points.name: anorexia nervosa
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The basic symptoms that result in a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa are being at significantly low weight for one’s age and size, an intense fear of fat and food, and a distorted body image.
knowledge_points.plain: 害怕发胖而自我饥饿

knowledge_points.name: bulimia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Bulimia commonly involves a binge-purge cycle in which sufferers eat large quantities of food and then attempt to purge the food from their bodies by throwing up or using laxatives.
knowledge_points.plain: 暴食后催吐或导泻

knowledge_points.name: binge-eating disorder
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Binge-eating disorder is thought to be the most commonly occurring eating disorder in the United States. It involves eating very large quantities of food in a short time while experiencing feelings of loss of control.
knowledge_points.plain: 短时间大量进食并失控

knowledge_points.name: Substance-related and addictive disorders
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Substance-related and addictive disorders is a diagnosis made when the use of such substances or behaviors, like gambling, regularly negatively affects a person’s life.
knowledge_points.plain: 物质使用造成负面影响的诊断

knowledge_points.name: diagnostic labels
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, keep in mind that diagnostic labels are not always correct and tend to outlast their usefulness.
knowledge_points.plain: 诊断标签可能不准确

sections.section: The Advantages and Disadvantages of Diagnostic Labels

knowledge_points.name: The Rosenhan study
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In 1978, David Rosenhan conducted a study in which he and several associates sought admission to a number of mental hospitals.
knowledge_points.plain: 假病人入住精神病院的研究

knowledge_points.name: methods of treatment
knowledge_points.definition_quote: All the methods of treatment, however, share a common purpose: to alter the client’s behavior, thoughts, and/or feelings.
knowledge_points.plain: 治疗旨在改变行为想法或感受

knowledge_points.name: Psychotherapies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychotherapies, except for behavioral treatments, largely consist of talking to a psychologist.
knowledge_points.plain: 主要通过谈话进行的心理治疗

knowledge_points.name: Psychoanalysis
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychoanalysis is a therapeutic technique developed by Sigmund Freud.
knowledge_points.plain: 弗洛伊德创立的精神分析疗法

knowledge_points.name: Psychodynamic therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychodynamic therapy grew out of Sigmund Freud’s psychoanalytic approach.
knowledge_points.plain: 源于精神分析的心理动力疗法

knowledge_points.name: Symptom substitution
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Symptom substitution is when, after a person has been successfully treated for one psychological disorder, that person begins to experience a new psychological problem.
knowledge_points.plain: 治愈后出现新的心理问题

knowledge_points.name: Free association
knowledge_points.definition_quote: More commonly, psychodynamic theorists might ask patients to free associate—to say whatever comes to mind without thinking.
knowledge_points.plain: 不假思索说出脑中一切

knowledge_points.name: Manifest content
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In dream analysis, what the patient reports is called the manifest content of the dream.
knowledge_points.plain: 梦中表面可见的内容

knowledge_points.name: Latent content
knowledge_points.definition_quote: What is really of interest to the analyst is the latent or hidden content.
knowledge_points.plain: 梦隐藏的真实含义

knowledge_points.name: Resistance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Since analysis can be a painful process of coming to terms with deeply repressed, troubling thoughts, people are thought to try to protect themselves through resistance.
knowledge_points.plain: 抗拒触及压抑的痛苦想法

knowledge_points.name: Transference
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Transference is when, during therapy, patients begin to have strong feelings toward their therapists.
knowledge_points.plain: 把情感转移到治疗师身上

knowledge_points.name: Insight therapies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Insight therapies highlight the importance of the patients/clients gaining an understanding of their problems.
knowledge_points.plain: 强调领悟问题本质的疗法

knowledge_points.name: Humanistic therapies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Humanistic therapies focus on helping people to understand and accept themselves and strive to self-actualize.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助人接纳自我并自我实现

knowledge_points.name: Self-actualization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-actualization means to reach one’s highest potential.
knowledge_points.plain: 发挥最高潜能

knowledge_points.name: Determinism
knowledge_points.definition_quote: It holds that people have no influence over what happens to them and that their choices are predetermined by forces outside of their control.
knowledge_points.plain: 行为由外部力量决定

knowledge_points.name: Person-centered therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This therapeutic method hinges on the therapist providing the client with what Rogers termed unconditional positive regard.
knowledge_points.plain: 以无条件积极关注为核心

knowledge_points.name: Unconditional positive regard
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Unconditional positive regard is blanket acceptance and support of a person regardless of what the person says or does.
knowledge_points.plain: 无条件接纳与支持来访者

knowledge_points.name: Active listening
knowledge_points.definition_quote: They encourage the clients to talk a lot about how they feel and sometimes mirror back those feelings to help clarify the feelings for the client.
knowledge_points.plain: 倾听并回映来访者感受

knowledge_points.name: Gestalt therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another type of humanistic therapy is Gestalt therapy, developed by Fritz Perls.
knowledge_points.plain: 强调整个自我与当下

knowledge_points.name: Existential therapies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Existential therapies are humanistic therapies that focus on helping clients achieve a subjectively meaningful perception of their lives.
knowledge_points.plain: 帮助来访者寻找生活意义

knowledge_points.name: Applied behavior analysis (ABA)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One behavioral approach, most used to help people with developmental disorders like autism spectrum disorder, is known as applied behavior analysis (ABA).
knowledge_points.plain: 用强化系统塑造行为

knowledge_points.name: Counterconditioning
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One technique is counterconditioning, a kind of classical conditioning in which an unpleasant conditioned response is replaced with a pleasant one.
knowledge_points.plain: 用愉快反应替代不愉快反应

knowledge_points.name: Systematic desensitization
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This process involves teaching the client to replace the feelings of anxiety with relaxation.
knowledge_points.plain: 逐步放松以消除焦虑

knowledge_points.name: Anxiety hierarchy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An anxiety hierarchy is a rank-ordered list of what the client fears, starting with the least frightening and ending with the most frightening.
knowledge_points.plain: 按恐惧程度排列的清单

knowledge_points.name: Flooding
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Unlike the gradual process of systematic desensitization, flooding involves having the client address the most frightening scenario first.
knowledge_points.plain: 直接面对最恐惧的情境

knowledge_points.name: Modeling
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Modeling, as you will recall from Unit 3, is a process through which one person learns by observing and then imitating the behavior of another.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过观察模仿他人学习

knowledge_points.name: Exposure therapies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: However, discussing it with systematic desensitization and flooding makes sense because all three are exposure therapies; all involve some degree of contact with the feared stimuli.
knowledge_points.plain: 让来访者接触恐惧刺激

knowledge_points.name: Aversive therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This process involves pairing a habit a person wishes to break, such as smoking or bed- wetting, with an unpleasant stimulus such as electric shock or nausea.
knowledge_points.plain: 将坏习惯与厌恶刺激配对

knowledge_points.name: Token economy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: In a token economy, desired behaviors are identified and rewarded with tokens.
knowledge_points.plain: 用代币奖励期望行为

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: As cognitive therapists locate the cause of psychological problems in the way people think, their methods of therapy concentrate on changing these unhealthy thought patterns.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过改变思维模式治疗

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive restructuring
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The goal of cognitive therapy is often referred to as cognitive restructuring, which involves challenging people’s patterns of maladaptive thinking.
knowledge_points.plain: 挑战适应不良的思维

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive triad
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Beck explains depression using the cognitive triad: people’s beliefs about themselves, their worlds, and their futures.
knowledge_points.plain: 对自我世界未来的消极信念

knowledge_points.name: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: One popular group of therapies combines the ideas and techniques of both cognitive and behavioral psychologists. This approach to therapy is known as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
knowledge_points.plain: 结合认知与行为技术

knowledge_points.name: Rational emotive behavior therapy (REBT)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Therapists employing REBT look to expose and confront the dysfunctional thoughts of their clients.
knowledge_points.plain: 驳斥不合理信念的疗法

knowledge_points.name: Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: DBT focuses more on emotions than thought patterns and is often used to help people who have extreme emotional reactions interact with others and their environments in healthier ways.
knowledge_points.plain: 侧重情绪调节的认知行为疗法

knowledge_points.name: Group therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Sometimes group therapy involves meeting with several people experiencing similar difficulties.
knowledge_points.plain: 多人同时接受心理治疗

knowledge_points.name: Family therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Since a client’s problems do not occur in a vacuum, many therapists find meeting with the whole family helpful in revealing the patterns of interaction among family members and altering the behavior of the whole family rather than just one member.
knowledge_points.plain: 以整个家庭为单位的治疗

knowledge_points.name: Self-help groups
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Self-help groups such as Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) are a form of group therapy that does not involve a therapist at all.
knowledge_points.plain: 无治疗师带领的互助团体

knowledge_points.name: Somatic therapies
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Therefore, these psychologists advocate the use of somatic therapies—therapies that produce bodily changes.
knowledge_points.plain: 通过身体改变治疗心理障碍

knowledge_points.name: Drug therapy or psychopharmacology
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The most common type of somatic therapy is drug therapy or psychopharmacology, also known as chemotherapy (see Table 18.2).
knowledge_points.plain: 用药物治疗心理障碍

knowledge_points.name: Antipsychotic medications
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Schizophrenia is generally treated with antipsychotic medications such as Thorazine or Haldol. These drugs generally function by blocking the receptor sites for dopamine.
knowledge_points.plain: 阻断多巴胺受体

knowledge_points.name: Tardive dyskinesia
knowledge_points.definition_quote: An unfortunate side effect of antipsychotic medication is tardive dyskinesia—Parkinsonian-like, chronic muscle tremors.
knowledge_points.plain: 抗精神病药致肌肉震颤

knowledge_points.name: serotonin selective reuptake inhibitor drugs (SSRIs)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The three most common kinds of drugs used to treat unipolar depression are tricyclic antidepressants, monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors, and serotonin selective reuptake inhibitor drugs or SSRIs (most notably Prozac).
knowledge_points.plain: 提高血清素活动的抗抑郁药

knowledge_points.name: Lithium
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Lithium, a metal, is often used to treat the manic phase of bipolar disorder.
knowledge_points.plain: 治疗躁狂发作的金属药物

knowledge_points.name: Biofeedback
knowledge_points.definition_quote: During biofeedback, a patient is taught to recognize and then control various physiological responses such as breathing, heart rate, or even brain activity (neurofeedback) without medication.
knowledge_points.plain: 学习控制生理反应

knowledge_points.name: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) employs magnets to alter brain activity and is mainly used in the treatment of depression.
knowledge_points.plain: 用磁刺激改变脑活动

knowledge_points.name: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Another approach targeted at changing brain activity is electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).
knowledge_points.plain: 电击诱发短暂癫痫发作

knowledge_points.name: Psychosurgery
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychosurgery involves the purposeful destruction of part of the brain to alter a person’s behavior.
knowledge_points.plain: 破坏部分脑组织以改变行为

knowledge_points.name: Prefrontal lobotomy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: This operation involved cutting the main neurons leading to the frontal lobe of the brain.
knowledge_points.plain: 切断通往额叶的神经元

knowledge_points.name: Eclectic therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Many therapists do not exclusively use one type of therapy.
knowledge_points.plain: 综合使用多种疗法

knowledge_points.name: Somatic cognitive therapy
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Somatic cognitive therapy is another very common combination eclectic therapy.
knowledge_points.plain: 药物与认知谈话治疗结合

knowledge_points.name: Psychiatrists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Psychiatrists are medical doctors and are therefore the only therapists permitted to prescribe medication in most U.S. states.
knowledge_points.plain: 可开药的医学博士

knowledge_points.name: Clinical psychologists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Clinical psychologists earn doctoral degrees (PhDs) that require four or more years of study.
knowledge_points.plain: 获得博士学位的心理学家

knowledge_points.name: Counseling therapists
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Counseling therapists or counseling psychotherapists typically have some kind of graduate degree in psychology.
knowledge_points.plain: 处理较轻问题的咨询师

knowledge_points.name: therapeutic alliance
knowledge_points.definition_quote: The success of the treatment process is also clearly affected by the relationship between client and therapist—the therapeutic alliance.
knowledge_points.plain: 来访者与治疗师的关系

knowledge_points.name: Evidence-based interventions
knowledge_points.definition_quote: Evidence-based interventions have been demonstrated to work through research, but even these approaches will not be effective for everyone all the time.
knowledge_points.plain: 经研究证实有效的干预
